2.3.2

This is a security release fixing several security relevant issues.

Changelog

Sourced from picomatch's changelog.

Release history

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

  • Changelogs are for humans, not machines.
  • There should be an entry for every single version.
  • The same types of changes should be grouped.
  • Versions and sections should be linkable.
  • The latest version comes first.
  • The release date of each versions is displayed.
  • Mention whether you follow Semantic Versioning.

Changelog entries are classified using the following labels (from keep-a-changelog):

  • Added for new features.
  • Changed for changes in existing functionality.
  • Deprecated for soon-to-be removed features.
  • Removed for now removed features.
  • Fixed for any bug fixes.
  • Security in case of vulnerabilities.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

reviews.body:
## Status — merging to `dev`, not production-ready

This PR is being merged into `dev` (integration branch) rather than `main` because the **feature is not fully functional end-to-end yet**. Production readiness requires three deferred follow-ups, none of which are in scope here:

| Gap | Why it blocks default-on | Tracking |
|---|---|---|
| **Adapter heartbeat plumbing** | LangGraph / CrewAI / AutoGen / CCSStore don't yet call `coordinator.record_heartbeat(...)` or expose `recover()`. Without that, real-adapter use of `enabled=True` would false-reclaim immediately under any normal compute. | `docs/plans/2026-05-07-002-feat-adapter-heartbeat-plumbing-plan.md` (planned, not started) |
| **TLA+ amendment (origin Gate 1)** | Invariants I1–I7 in `docs/specs/crash-recovery.md` need formal verification before the flag flips default-on. | Separate backlog item |
| **End-user durability narrative** | Operator-facing docs explaining the "coherence ≠ durability" contract (D3 discards uncommitted MODIFIED). | Origin Carryover Risk #4 |

**What this PR ships safely to dev:** the coordinator-side machinery behind `crash_recovery.enabled=False` (default). Existing scenarios produce byte-identical state-transition logs to the v0.5 baseline (R5/I7). No behavioral change for any current consumer until an operator opts in.

The branching strategy that drives this choice is documented in the local `CLAUDE.md` (gitignored): feature work integrates to `dev`; `dev → main` is a separate release merge.

**Note on diff scope:** the PR includes a 1-line `README.md` addition that exists on `main` but not yet on `dev` (a "coherence gap evidence brief" link from a prior `main`-side commit). It will collapse out automatically once `main → dev` is synced; included here only because of the merge-base differential. All other diff content is the crash-recovery work.

---

## Summary

Coordinator-side crash recovery for stale `MODIFIED` / `EXCLUSIVE` MESI grants. `enforce_transient_timeouts` already handles transient states; this adds `enforce_stable_grant_timeouts` for stable-state grants held by crashed or livelocked agents. Ships behind a feature flag (`enabled=False` default).

Closes the liveness gap behind backlog item C: two validated leads (jingchang0623 OOM-kill cron, jessieibarra checkpoint-restore short-circuit) at pain=7 each.

## Implementation (12 commits)

| Phase | Commits | Net |
|---|---:|---|
| 6 implementation units | 6 | Coordinator + simulation wiring + benchmark scenario; 269 tests |
| Code-review polish (safe-auto) | 1 | 9 fixes, no behavior change |
| Code-review P1 fixes | 2 | `kill`×`busy` resurrection bug; log-fail bookkeeping inconsistency |
| Code-review P2 fixes | 2 | `>` vs `>=` operator asymmetry; `ttl_ticks=0` silent-skip |
| Manual test additions | 1 | Coverage for defensive branch, restore-resumes-heartbeat, double-run determinism |

**Total:** +1900 / −16 lines (after review-driven additions). 282 tests passing (was 223 pre-branch — +59 tests).

## Key behavior

- **Hybrid liveness signal:** per-agent heartbeat (catches hard crashes) + per-grant max-hold (catches livelocks).
- **Trigger ordering:** `reclaim_heartbeat` checked first; both conditions use `>=` for symmetry.
- **Sweep ordering:** transient sweep runs first, stable sweep takes its snapshot afterward; a given (agent, artifact) is reclaimed by at most one sweep per tick.
- **Reclamation-aware commit:** stale agents calling `commit()` get `reclaimed_by=<trigger> at_tick=<n>` in the error message; the slot survives a `SHARED` transition (jessieibarra path) and clears only on M∪E re-acquire.
- **Tick monotonicity (R12):** `record_heartbeat` uses `max(prev, incoming)` — out-of-order delivery is harmless.
- **Composition fail-fast (R11):** refuses `enabled=True` startup when a strategy with inspectable `ttl_ticks` would have `max_hold_ticks <= ttl_ticks`. Distinguishes `ttl=None` (silent accept), integer `ttl` (validate, including `ttl=0`), and non-integer `ttl` (`RuntimeWarning`).
- **First-class `_killed_agents`:** failure-injection vocabulary distinguishes `kill` (permanent until explicit `restore`) from `busy` (auto-expires); `busy` on a killed agent raises strict `ValueError`.

## Test plan

- [x] 282 tests passing (was 223 pre-branch — +59 across 5 files)
- [x] Architecture boundary check (`tools/check_architecture.py`) clean
- [x] README benchmark numbers up-to-date (no benchmark drift)
- [x] **R5 byte-identity preserved:** state-transition log byte-identical to v0.5 baseline when `enabled=False` (instance-id-normalized regression test)
- [x] **R6 observability:** `validate_log` reports no gaps or schema mismatches under the new code paths
- [x] **R8 jessieibarra path:** dedicated test asserts the reclamation slot survives `INVALID → SHARED` and a late `commit()` raises with the diagnostic message
- [x] **R9 combined scenario:** `benchmarks/scenarios/crash_recovery_validation.yaml` exercises OOM-kill (`reclaim_heartbeat`), checkpoint-restore-then-commit (`reclaim_heartbeat` + diagnostic message), AND live-but-stuck max-hold (`reclaim_max_hold`) in one deterministic run
- [x] Trigger ordering, sweep ordering, `granted_at_tick` lifecycle, `kill`/`busy`/`restore` semantics
- [x] Boundary tests for heartbeat-stale at exact timeout (`>=`)
- [x] Log-emit-failure consistency: state and bookkeeping stay aligned when `state_log` raises
- [x] Double-run determinism for the combined scenario

## Code review summary

11 reviewers ran (correctness, testing, maintainability, project-standards, agent-native, learnings + adversarial, performance, api-contract, reliability, kieran-python). Verdict went from "Ready with fixes" to "Ready to merge to dev" after the gated-auto P1/P2 fixes and manual test additions landed.

| Class | Count | Status |
|---|---:|---|
| safe_auto applied | 9 | committed |
| gated_auto P1 fixed | 2 | committed (`kill`×`busy` resurrection; log-fail bookkeeping) |
| gated_auto P2 fixed | 2 | committed (`>`/`>=` asymmetry; `ttl_ticks=0` silent-skip) |
| manual tests added | 4 | committed |
| advisory (informational) | 7 | left in report; included in this PR's notes |

## Notes for reviewers

- All planning artifacts (`docs/brainstorms/`, `docs/plans/`, `docs/specs/`) are gitignored locally per the repo's `.git/info/exclude` policy. They are NOT in this PR. The spec doc (`docs/specs/crash-recovery.md`) lives on the author's clone.
- Default behavior is unchanged: `crash_recovery.enabled=False` is the default; existing scenarios produce byte-identical state logs to the v0.5 baseline.
- The `stable_grant_reclamations` field added to `SimulationMetrics` is a metric-schema addition (intentional). On flag-off scenarios it's always `0`.
- `benchmarks/expected.json` is NOT regenerated — its schema is LangGraph workload token counts, unrelated to `SimulationMetrics`.
- The `dev → main` promotion will happen after the adapter plumbing PR lands and the TLA+ amendment is merged.

reviews.body:
## Description

Closes #38262 (depends on #38089, already merged).

Once the Inventory Sync migration to `inventory_sync_server` (the asynchronous, `remoted`-relayed
`POST /stateful` pipeline) was complete, this PR does the cleanup and adaptation work the
migration issue left open:

1. **Adapts and substantially extends** `tools/manager_benchmark`, the load-generation suite that
   exercises the new HTTPS-relayed pipeline, so it can reproduce a real agent's wire (zstd
   compression, retry-on-`503`), replay real captured payloads, and assert its response contracts
   automatically (`expected` blocks) instead of only reporting numbers.
2. **Physically removes the legacy `inventory_sync` module**, which had been out of the build
   since the migration but still sat in the tree (~213 files, including its old benchmark and QA
   suites), together with its `modulesd` shim, its CI steps, and one dead installer block.
3. **Synchronizes the module's documentation** — the official `docs/ref` reference, the in-tree
   developer README, and the `internal_options.conf` template — with what `inventory_sync_server`
   actually does today, correcting a factual error in the configuration reference and filling in
   the requirements/design-decision context the migration's design corpus never shipped with the
   code.

## Proposed Changes

### Benchmark load generator (`tools/manager_benchmark`)

- Added agent-like `503` retry (scenario-tunable `retry` block: interval, bounded attempts,
  disabled in the shed-counting scenarios) and real event-rate pacing for engine lanes
  (`events_per_second` / `events_per_batch`), replacing the request-rate `max_eps`.
- Added an optional per-scenario `expected` block: hardware-independent counter assertions
  evaluated after the run (exit code `3` on failure), turning the contract scenarios into
  CI-usable checks instead of numbers a human has to eyeball.
- Added `zstd` request compression, on by default in agent mode like a real 5.x agent
  (`defaults.compression` per scenario or `--compression` per run).
- Added the `real_first_connect` / `real_first_connect_uds` scenarios: a freshly connected Windows
  and Linux agent replaying their first-connection captures at full fidelity, including the
  27,726-document Windows FIM registry corpus (~26 MB in one session) — rescued from the legacy
  benchmark into a zstd-compressed dump corpus before its removal.
- Recalibrated `contract_ramp_503` to trigger backpressure shedding regardless of hardware: its
  original fixed-session-count design produced zero `503`s on fast hardware; rebuilt as a
  fixed-duration unpaced flood of larger sessions, verified against `GET /metrics` to trip the
  intended admission gate, with an `expected` assertion so a future regression fails the run
  instead of passing silently.
- Added `--keep-agents` to `run_benchmark.sh` / `run_matrix.sh`, opting an agent-mode run out of
  the unconditional pre-run cleanup so a run's agents and indexed documents survive long enough to
  inspect in the indexer's dashboard.
- Added the `real_inspect_fleet` scenario: a dashboard-inspection showcase pairing one Windows and
  one Linux agent across every real inventory module plus a basic engine lane, kept connected on
  `/control` keepalives for several minutes after the inventory sessions land.
- New Go unit tests: pacing/duration parsing, scenario-schema validation, zstd round-trip, the
  real-payload dump loader, and `expected`-block verdict evaluation.

### Legacy module removal

- Removed `src/wazuh_modules/inventory_sync/` in full (sources, its old QA suite, its old
  benchmark) — `inventory_sync_server` replaced it and the module had already been out of the
  build (`add_subdirectory` commented out) since the migration.
- Removed the `wm_inventory_sync` `modulesd` C shim and its (already-commented-out) registration.
- Relocated the one struct the legacy tree still contributed (`context.hpp`) into
  `vulnerability_scanner`, its only real consumer, updating the two unit tests that included it by
  path.
- Removed the CI steps and path filters that still referenced the legacy module: a
  `clang-format` lint step, path triggers on `5_testintegration_vulnerability-scanner.yml`, and
  negative path filters on five macOS/Windows component-test workflows.
- Removed the installer's dead `libinventory_sync.so` install block (`src/init/inst-functions.sh`)
  and the corresponding `CODEOWNERS` entry.
- Reworded comments across `remoted`, `keystore_server`, `vulnerability_scanner` and
  `inventory_sync_server` that cited the now-deleted paths or described the legacy module as
  current.

### Documentation

- Rewrote the architecture diagrams (the manager-wide one and the vulnerability-scanner one) to
  draw the real pipeline — `remoted` relaying `POST /stateful` over UDS to `inventory_sync_server`
  with an in-process VD scan lane — instead of the retired Router topic and per-session RocksDB.
- Corrected the `inventory-sync-server` configuration reference: `max_body_size` has no 16 MiB
  default (the effective cap derives from the in-flight byte budget), and documented five
  previously-undocumented options (`sync_workers`, `sync_queue_bytes`,
  `vd_feed_retry_after_seconds`, `vd_workers`, `vd_scan_queue_slots`) and the module's four
  distinct `503` gates.
- Added the module's full tunable set (~28 options) to the `etc/wazuh-manager-internal-options.conf`
  template, every entry commented out at its compiled default — behavior-neutral.
- Synchronized three documentation layers so the design context ships with the code: the in-tree
  developer README now carries the migration's complete requirements catalog (functional,
  non-functional, indexer-connector synchronization and VD-handoff families, each flagged
  kept/superseded), the full design-decision catalog (D1–D22), the annotated `FullSession` schema,
  an end-to-end admission diagram naming every `503` gate, a developer FAQ, and a benchmark
  section; the official `docs/ref` pages gained use cases, an operations FAQ, and cross-references
  to the in-tree README and the benchmark harness (which links back in kind).

### Results and Evidence

Verified locally against a live manager on this branch:

- Full `TARGET=manager` build succeeds after the legacy removal.
- `vulnerability_scanner_unit_tests`: 465/465 passed. `inventory_sync_server_utest`: 318/318 passed.
- Live smoke: reinstalled the manager; all 8 daemons up; the module's boot log shows the expected
  routes, worker count and indexer reachability; only `libinventory_sync_server.so` gets installed.
- Benchmark smoke: `real_syscollector_debian` (uds) — 48/48 sessions ok, exit `0` (VALID).
- `real_inspect_fleet` (agent mode) run end to end: 14/14 sessions ok, the scenario's `expected`
  block passed (`documents_sent == 31950`), both agents stayed connected on `/control` keepalives
  for ~9m48s before disconnecting as designed; the indexed document counts per index (FIM registry
  keys/values, SCA, VD vulnerabilities, etc.) were spot-checked directly against the indexer and
  matched.
- `pr-clang.sh --check` clean on every file this PR touches.
- `mdbook build` on the documentation tree completes with no new errors or warnings.
- This branch was rebased onto the updated `5.0.0-https` base (7/7 commits replayed with zero
  conflicts); a diff against a pre-rebase backup branch showed the change set unaffected beyond the
  base's own unrelated commits.

### Manual tests with their corresponding evidence

<!-- Minimum checks required depending on if it is Agent or Manager related -->
- Compilation without warnings on every supported platform
  - [ ] Linux
  - [ ] Windows _(N/A — this module builds only for `TARGET=manager`, which does not target Windows)_
  - [ ] MAC OS X _(N/A — the manager does not ship for macOS; the macOS workflows this PR touches build the agent only)_
- [ ] Log syntax and correct language review

<!-- Depending on the affected OS -->
- Memory tests for Linux
  - [ ] Coverity
  - [ ] Valgrind (memcheck and descriptor leaks check)
  - [ ] AddressSanitizer
- Memory tests for Windows
  - [ ] Coverity _(N/A — manager-only change, not built for Windows)_
  - [ ] UMDH _(N/A — manager-only change, not built for Windows)_
- Memory tests for macOS
  - [ ] Leaks _(N/A — manager-only change, not built for macOS)_
  - [ ] AddressSanitizer _(N/A — manager-only change, not built for macOS)_

- Decoder/Rule tests _(Wazuh v4.x)_
  - [ ] Added unit testing files ".ini" _(N/A — no decoders or rules changed)_
  - [ ] `runtests.py` executed without errors _(N/A — no decoders or rules changed)_

- Engine _(Wazuh v5.x and above)_
  - [ ] Test run in parallel _(N/A — the Engine itself is not touched by this PR)_
  - [ ] ASAN for test (utest/ctest) _(N/A — the Engine itself is not touched by this PR)_
  - [ ] TSAN for test and wazuh-engine. _(N/A — the Engine itself is not touched by this PR)_

- Wazuh server API/Framework
  - [ ] Run API Integration Tests _(N/A — no API/Framework code changed)_

### Artifacts Affected

- `libinventory_sync_server.so` remains the only shared library modulesd loads for this module;
  `libinventory_sync.so` (legacy) is no longer produced or installed.
- CI workflows: `5_codelinter_clangformat.yml`, `5_testintegration_vulnerability-scanner.yml`,
  `5_testcomponent_build-macos.yml`, `5_testcomponent_windows-dll-hijack.yml`,
  `5_testcomponent_windows-files.yml`, `5_testcomponent_windows-installer-upgrade.yml`,
  `5_testunit_macos.yml` — legacy path filters/steps removed, no behavior change for the current
  module.
- `.github/CODEOWNERS` — the legacy path entry replaced with `inventory_sync_server`.
- `src/init/inst-functions.sh` — dropped a dead install step (the legacy `.so` it guarded on never
  exists in a build from this branch).
- `tools/manager_benchmark/` gained new scenario files and a `sample_payloads/dumps/first_connect/`
  dump corpus (zstd-compressed, real captured payloads).

### Configuration Changes

- `etc/wazuh-manager-internal-options.conf`: added a new commented-out section documenting all
  `wazuh_modules.inventory_sync_server_*` options with their compiled defaults and ranges. No
  option's default changed — every added line matches the code's own default, so an unmodified
  install behaves identically before and after this PR.
- No manager-facing configuration option was added, removed, or had its default changed.

### Tests Introduced

- Go unit tests in `tools/manager_benchmark/tool_simulator/internal/`: `pacing_test.go` (duration
  parsing), `scenario/scenario_test.go` (schema validation), `wire/zstd_test.go` (compression
  round-trip), `source/dump_test.go` (real-payload dump loading), `verdict/verdict_test.go` (the
  new `expected`-block evaluator).
- `src/wazuh_modules/vulnerability_scanner/tests/unit/eventGetCve_test.cpp` and
  `vulnerabilityScannerFacade_test.cpp`: updated to include the relocated `context.hpp` by its new
  path — no behavior change, existing coverage preserved.
- `src/wazuh_modules/inventory_sync_server/testtool/CMakeLists.txt`: removed a dead legacy include
  path left over from the module's own migration.

## Review Checklist

- [ ] Code changes reviewed
- [ ] Relevant evidence provided
- [ ] Tests cover the new functionality
- [ ] Configuration changes documented
- [ ] Developer documentation reflects the changes
- [ ] Meets requirements and/or definition of done
- [ ] No unresolved dependencies with other issues
- [ ] ...

Bumps the npm_and_yarn group with 2 updates in the /src/frontend directory: [lodash-es](https://github.com/lodash/lodash) and [vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/HEAD/packages/vite). Updates `lodash-es` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash-es's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template

  • 59be2de release(minor): bump to 4.18.0 (#6161)
  • af63457 fix: broken tests for _.template 879aaa9
  • 1073a76 fix: linting issues
  • 879aaa9 fix: validate imports keys in _.template
  • fe8d32e fix: block prototype pollution in baseUnset via constructor/prototype traversal

Updates `hono` from 4.12.9 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `hono` from 4.12.8 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

  • lodash.orderby
  • lodash.tonumber
  • lodash.trim
  • lodash.trimend
  • lodash.sortedindexby
  • lodash.zipobjectdeep
  • lodash.unset
  • lodash.omit
  • lodash.template

retrieval; verified with a real failing-before/passing-after test; closed
out truthfully in Ukrainian; and the instance itself audited for integrity
from its own bundle.

This PR has been through three independent hardening reviews since it was
opened (2026-07-15). Each found real gaps between what the slice claimed
and what it actually did, and each was fixed in place rather than papered
over - see the commit history for the full per-round detail (`efc6736`
"heal the vertical slice", `f0cc722` "round 2 hardening", `d875293`/`fa29175`
"round 3 hardening"). This description reflects the **current, final**
state only - stale round-1/round-2 commands, counts, and open items have
been removed rather than layered.

## Architecture (current)

- **Config/lock split.** `.eif/config.yaml` is user-owned (project name,
  adapter, locale, governance) and is never touched by a routine upgrade.
  `.eif/framework.lock.yaml` is EIF-managed provenance (exact framework
  commit, dirty flag, `ref_verification: git-verified|asserted`, a
  sha256-hashed bundle manifest with a combined digest, the generated
  adapter entrypoint), fully regenerated every init/upgrade. See
  [`docs/architecture/instance-contract.md`](docs/architecture/instance-contract.md).
- **Three explicit modes, decided by what's on disk, not by which flags
  happen to be passed.** `init` (no config yet, `--project-name`
  required); `upgrade` (config exists, no `--force` - project/adapter/
  locale/migration-status all come from the existing config and lock;
  any of those flags passed anyway are ignored with a printed note, never
  silently applied); `reconfigure` (`--force` - an explicit flag wins,
  anything unpassed keeps its current value, existing config backed up
  first).
- **One transaction for the full managed state.** Config (when written),
  runtime bundle, lock, entrypoint, and `.gitignore` each stage to a
  `.next` path and commit as one ordered sequence of atomic renames. If
  any stage fails, every already-committed stage in that run rolls back
  to its exact prior content, and any staged-but-never-reached `.next`
  file is cleaned up - not just the runtime swap, and not just a
  preflight check.
- **Marker-safe entrypoint/`.gitignore` merges.** `CLAUDE.md` and
  `.gitignore` updates go through `eif_markers.py`, which refuses to
  write anything if the existing `BEGIN`/`END` markers are missing a
  partner, reversed, or duplicated, instead of silently corrupting
  content around them.
- **Self-verification.** `scripts/eif_verify_runtime.py`, bundled into
  every instance, checks config/lock schema validity, manifest digest
  self-consistency, every manifested file's hash, missing/unexpected
  files (`README.md`/`__pycache__` excluded by design), config/adapter-
  registry/lock/entrypoint consistency, provenance notes, and marker
  integrity, in one pass, from the instance's own bundle.
- **Truthful rendering.** `scripts/eif_render.py` reads
  `documentation_locale` from `.eif/config.yaml` by default and writes
  real files. A config that exists but is broken fails loudly instead of
  silently rendering in English (a missing config is a different,
  legitimate case). A "final" render with any unresolved `{placeholder}`
  fails by default; `--draft` explicitly opts into a partial render.
  Writes are atomic.
- **Lifecycle- and schema-aware retrieval.** `eif_search_knowledge.py`
  returns only eligible statuses by default and reports unparseable-YAML,
  schema-invalid, and status-ineligible as three distinct outcomes, never
  confused with "no results." The generated `CLAUDE.md` search command
  includes `--framework-root` by default.
- **Restricted adapter registry.** `--adapter` only accepts a registered
  name (`scripts/eif_adapters.py`); `eif_init` generates `CLAUDE.md` (the
  file Claude Code actually loads, per official docs) via that registry,
  not a hardcoded guess.

## Commands (current, all re-run this session)

```
# init
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path> --project-name <name> --locale uk
# routine upgrade - no flags needed, driven by the existing config/lock
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path>
# explicit reconfiguration - only the flags passed change anything
python scripts/eif_init.py --framework-root . --instance-path <path> --force --locale en

python .eif/runtime/eif_search_knowledge.py --knowledge-root knowledge --framework-root .eif/runtime "<query>"
python .eif/runtime/eif_verify_runtime.py --framework-root .eif/runtime
python .eif/runtime/eif_render.py --framework-root .eif/runtime knowledge-delta
python .eif/runtime/eif_render.py --framework-root .eif/runtime session-closeout --set task_name="..." --set branch_or_pr="..." --set verification_result="..." --set artifacts="..." --set promoted="..." --set not_done="..." --set open_questions="..."

python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --instance-root <path> "knowledge/**/*.md"
python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --config <path>/.eif/config.yaml
python scripts/eif_validate_frontmatter.py --framework-root . --lock <path>/.eif/framework.lock.yaml
python scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py --repo .
python scripts/eif_check_links.py --repo .
```

## Tests

11 suites, 234 checks, all passing locally and reproduced identically from
a fresh `git clone` to a temporary directory outside the repository:

`test_validate.py` 15, `test_privacy_scan.py` 19, `test_knowledge_delta.py`
6, `test_generate_index.py` 12, `test_search_knowledge.py` 11,
`test_locale.py` 7, `test_render.py` 22, `test_markers.py` 12,
`test_verify_runtime.py` 17, `test_init.py` 38, `test_journey.py` 75.

`test_journey.py` is a real subprocess journey (not internal-function
calls) covering: init/upgrade/reconfigure against a real seed project;
config/lock schema validation; runtime materialization; English +
Ukrainian retrieval; task-scope; a failing-before/passing-after behavioral
test; config-driven Ukrainian Knowledge Delta + closeout written to real
files; artifact/privacy/link validation from the instance's own bundle;
a routine upgrade proven to preserve a `migration_status: adopted` set by
an earlier explicit reconfigure, with zero flags on the upgrade itself;
the generated search command's `--framework-root`; strict-vs-`--draft`
rendering; `eif_verify_runtime.py` against a clean instance and against
each of: a hand-edited bundle file, a schema-invalid lock, and reversed
entrypoint markers; a second, fully independent instance; and, for each
of the four post-config transaction stages (runtime, lock, entrypoint,
`.gitignore`) in turn, a real injected failure immediately after that
stage commits, followed by confirming every already-committed stage
restored to its exact prior byte-for-byte content, zero orphaned
`.next`/`.previous` files, and the instance passing both
`eif_verify_runtime.py` and a real retrieval command afterward.

Also re-run from the clean clone: the demo's own behavioral test
(`examples/demo-workspace/tests/test_calendar_utils.py`), a privacy scan
and link check (0 findings, both empty), and a YAML/JSON-Schema
self-consistency check over every schema file.

CI on the current head (`fa29175`): **6/6 jobs green** - Privacy scan,
Frontmatter and config schema validation, Vertical slice, Relative link
check, YAML and JSON Schema syntax check, Knowledge Delta completeness.

## Adapter evidence

`adapters/claude-code/README.md`. Claude Code CLI `2.1.169`, verified live
2026-07-15. Official docs confirm Claude Code loads `CLAUDE.md` at session
start. Persistent-instruction and skill discovery OBSERVED directly in the
sessions that built this slice. Hook rewrite behavior is **not**
re-verified end-to-end this round - carried over from the private
instance's dated (2026-06-16) evidence, with a note on what
re-verification would require. No hook scripts shipped (out of scope).
Every command above runs with zero dependency on any hook.

## Ukrainian locale evidence

Three real output surfaces: status messages (`eif_init.py`, e.g.
`Ініціалізація EIF project instance у ...`), Knowledge Delta
(`examples/demo-workspace/knowledge-delta.md`), and closeout
(`examples/demo-workspace/session-closeout.md`), all rendered by the
config-driven command above with no `--locale` flag. English fallback
verified for both "no config" and "unknown locale" - distinct from a
broken config, which now fails loudly instead of silently defaulting to
English. Framework identifiers, schemas, commands, and code stay English
throughout. **D-06/D-07 remain open** - this slice is evidence for that
future decision, not a substitute for it.

## Privacy statement

`python scripts/eif_privacy_scan.py --repo .` against the final tree, and
independently against the clean clone: 0 absolute-path leaks, 0
secret-shaped findings, 0 denylisted-token findings, both times. No
private repository names, machine paths, or owner-identifying detail were
introduced.

## Knowledge Delta

### New facts
- A routine upgrade that silently applies CLI defaults instead of the
  existing config is a real, severe bug class, not a hypothetical -
  reproduced live this round: a bare re-run without repeating
  `--locale`/`--migration-status` reset both to CLI defaults and
  overwrote `migration_status: adopted` with `greenfield` in the
  committed lock file.
- `os.replace()`/file rename is atomic on both POSIX and Windows, but a
  sequence of several such renames is not - the previous "transactional
  runtime swap" left the lock/entrypoint/`.gitignore` writes unprotected;
  a `_Stage`/`commit_transaction` primitive generalizes the same
  stage/commit/rollback shape to any file or directory.
- A schema's top-level `required` array and a nested object's own
  `required` array are independent - `framework-lock.schema.json` had
  `instance.migration_status` conditionally required only if `instance`
  itself was present, but `instance` was never in the top-level
  `required` list, so a lock missing the entire `instance` block passed
  schema validation. Found by a test written to be that specific negative
  case, not by manual review.

### New rules
- Do not let a schema-driven required field spread silently: when a
  schema gains a new required top-level object (here: `adapter` on
  `eif-config.schema.json`), every existing fixture/example/generated
  instance that predates it must be re-validated, not assumed still
  valid - a stale hand-written fixture (`scripts/tests/fixtures/config/
  positive.yaml`) and a stale generated instance
  (`examples/demo-workspace/.eif/framework.lock.yaml`, missing the new
  `ref_verification` field) both would have started failing silently
  otherwise; both caught before push by re-running the exact CI commands
  locally against a clean clone, not assumed from the suite's own
  internal test count.
- A test-only fault-injection env var, checked immediately after a stage
  commits (not before, not mid-rename), is a more honest and more
  reproducible way to prove rollback than a synthetic preflight failure -
  it exercises the real rollback code path at a real, named boundary
  instead of a code path that never reaches the transaction at all.

### Rejected hypotheses
- Considered enforcing `adapter.name` as a JSON Schema `enum` alongside
  the Python registry - rejected: two independently-maintained lists of
  the same valid values silently drift; kept the registry as the sole
  source of truth, cross-checked at runtime by `eif_verify_runtime.py`
  instead.
- Considered treating the marker-conflict refusal in `eif_init.py` as
  equivalent evidence to the transaction-rollback tests - rejected: one
  is a preflight refusal (nothing staged or written), the other is a
  mid-transaction rollback of already-committed stages; conflating them
  in the claims ledger would overstate what either test actually proves.

### Incidents
- None this round beyond the two staleness bugs already described under
  New rules (both fixed before push, neither reached CI red on the
  pushed commit).

### Promote to shared knowledge base?
[x] yes - the "routine upgrade must be driven by existing config, not CLI
defaults" lesson and the "a schema's nested `required` doesn't imply the
parent key is required" lesson are both general, not specific to this
framework. Not auto-promoted to `core/` - flagged for owner ratification,
consistent with the authority model's framework-vs-project scope
distinction.

### Updated knowledge files
- `docs/product/claims-evidence.md` (evidence, counts, and two new claim
  rows updated/added - see the diff)
- `README.md` (bootstrap-script and new self-verification capability rows
  updated)

## Claims evidence

`docs/product/claims-evidence.md` is the source of truth for what public
copy is allowed to say - updated this round with current test counts and
two new OBSERVED rows (config-driven upgrade + full transaction; instance
self-verification). Still **UNVERIFIED**: token savings, task-quality/
rework improvement. Still **NOT TESTED**: Graphify, RTK.

## Remaining open decisions

Unchanged by this PR - see `core/policies/decisions.md`: D-02, D-03, D-05
(CLI name - `eif_init.py` remains explicitly labeled experimental), D-06/
D-07 (language), D-08 (dependency model), D-09 (required adapters), D-10
through D-12 remain provisional/open.

## Deferred capabilities

Full execution-packet machinery, curator/active-learning, cross-repo
knowledge sync, a second adapter, Graphify, RTK - all explicitly out of
scope for this slice, not silently dropped. See the private migration
ledger (a private companion planning repository, PR #59, merged
2026-07-15 - not linked here since it contains private paths).

## Recommended next steps

Not started here, per this PR's own scope:
1. A real-project pilot (see the separate pilot-readiness proposal posted
   in this session's report - explicitly not the private companion planning repository).
2. Merge-gate hardening: explicit required-check names, `SKIPPED`/
   `NEUTRAL` treatment, unresolved-review-thread handling, override audit
   trail.
3. A second adapter, once the framework/adapter boundary has been proven
   to hold on a real pilot, not just in this synthetic demo.

Graphify/RTK integration, a quality-per-token benchmark, and public-ready
README/demo-recording/website work remain sequenced after those.

## Not merging

This agent will not merge this PR, per this task's explicit instruction.

`run_all.py` was trying to install and verify `editdistance` and `pandas` — both deliberately removed from `requirements.txt` and replaced with inline implementations — causing an immediate `FATAL` exit on every invocation.

## Core fix (`run_all.py`)

```python
# Before
_CRITICAL_INSTALL_PACKAGES = ["torch", "transformers", "datasets", "accelerate", "editdistance", "pandas"]
_CRITICAL_VERIFY_PACKAGES  = ["transformers", "datasets", "accelerate", "editdistance", "pandas"]

# After
_CRITICAL_INSTALL_PACKAGES = ["torch", "transformers", "datasets", "accelerate"]
_CRITICAL_VERIFY_PACKAGES  = ["transformers", "datasets", "accelerate"]
```

Also removed both packages from the debug version-printer block.

## Docs (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`)

- **Repo structure**: added all files now present (`benchmark_compare.py`, `cloud_pipeline.py`, `control_suite.py`, `dag_scheduler.py`, `dataset_normalizer.py`, `experiment_config_loader.py`, `hparam_search.py`, `logging_utils.py`, `memory_manager.py`, `multi_seed_runner.py`, `pipeline_critic.py`, `plot_convergence.py`, `preprocess_seller_split.py`, `resource_optimizer.py`, `startup_diagnostics.py`, `validators.py`); moved `paper.*` files under `paper/`; removed nonexistent `paper_mini.tex` and `train_donut.py`
- **Size/date**: monolith size 67 KB → 128 KB; terminal.txt example timestamps 2025 → 2026; `inject_results.py` example path updated to `paper/paper.tex`
- **Auto-install note**: explicitly lists which packages are checked (`torch`, `transformers`, `datasets`, `accelerate` — not `editdistance`/`pandas`)
- **Troubleshooting**: added `FATAL: editdistance` entry pointing to `git pull`
- **§ 4 GPU table**: clarified RTX 4090 row is the current workspace GPU
- **§ 5 Diagnostic table** + **§ 16 Known Issues**: added entry for this bug/fix
- **NED metric description**: removed stale `editdistance` package reference (inline implementation)

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Problem

Running `python run_all.py` fails with a fatal dependency error even on a fully-functional environment:

```
[setup] FATAL: The following packages could not be installed: editdistance
[setup] Run manually: pip install editdistance
```

And on the first attempt also:
```
[setup] FATAL: The following packages could not be installed: editdistance
[setup] Run manually: pip install editdistance
```

### Root Cause

`run_all.py` has two lists that are out of sync with `requirements.txt`:

```python
# run_all.py lines ~91-99
_CRITICAL_INSTALL_PACKAGES = [
    "torch",
    "transformers",
    "datasets",
    "accelerate",
    "editdistance",   # ← REMOVED from requirements.txt (inline replacement)
    "pandas",         # ← REMOVED from requirements.txt (inline replacement)
]
_CRITICAL_VERIFY_PACKAGES = ["transformers", "datasets", "accelerate", "editdistance", "pandas"]
```

`editdistance` was replaced by a 14-line inline Wagner-Fischer `_edit_distance()` in `donut_evaluator.py` and `benchmark_compare.py`. `pandas` was replaced by stdlib `csv`. Both were deliberately removed from `requirements.txt` with comments documenting the removal. However `run_all.py` still tries to install and verify them, causing:
1. An unnecessary pip install attempt every time
2. A FATAL error (exit code 2) after the restart because `editdistance` cannot install (or isn't in `requirements.txt`)
3. The pipeline never proceeds past the dependency-check phase

Additionally, `install_dependencies.py` is referenced in the CLAUDE.md header (pasted by user) but does not exist as a separate file — the functionality lives entirely within `run_all.py`. The docstrings inside `_install_dependencies()` also still mention `editdistance` as a dependency.

---

## Changes Required

### 1. `run_all.py` — Fix `_CRITICAL_INSTALL_PACKAGES` and `_CRITICAL_VERIFY_PACKAGES`

Remove `editdistance` and `pandas` from both lists (they are not in `requirements.txt` and have inline replacements):

```python
_CRITICAL_INSTALL_PACKAGES = [
    "torch",
    "transformers",
    "datasets",
    "accelerate",
    # editdistance → replaced with inline _edit_distance() in donut_evaluator.py
    # pandas → replaced with stdlib csv module
]
_CRITICAL_VERIFY_PACKAGES = ["transformers", "datasets", "accelerate"]
```

Also update the docstring of `_install_dependencies()` to remove the mention of `editdistance` and `pandas` from the critical packages list.

Also update the comment block at line ~96 area:
```python
# Before: "transformers, datasets, accelerate, editdistance, pandas"  
# After:  "transformers, datasets, accelerate"
```

Also update the `[startup]` summary printed near the beginning of `_verify_critical_packages` to not mention those removed packages.

### 2. `README.md` — Update dependency section and troubleshooting

In the **Dependency Reference** section (§ near the bottom), the "Removed — replaced with inline implementations" table already correctly documents `editdistance` as removed. However the **Quick Start** and **Auto-Install Features** text implies the auto-installer handles all critical deps — update to clarify:

- The auto-installer checks for: `torch`, `transformers`, `datasets`, `accelerate` (NOT `editdistance` or `pandas`)
- Add a note under **Troubleshooting** that if you see "FATAL: editdistance" you are on an older version and should `git pull` to get the fix
- Update the `terminal.txt` example in **Understanding the Output** — the example timestamp says `2025-02-28`; update the year reference to reflect 2026 runs
- Update the GPU timing note: the README says "~6–10 hours on a 96 GB GPU (RTX 6000 Blackwell)" — this is correct, keep it. But the file also says `run_all.py` is a "67 KB monolith" in the Roadmap — update to "128 KB monolith" to match the actual file size shown in the repo listing.
- The **Repository Structure** section lists `paper.tex`, `paper_mini.tex`, `presentation.tex`, `references.bib` in the root. These are actually in the `paper/` subdirectory per the CLAUDE.md repo structure — fix the listing to show them under `paper/`.
- Add `install_dependencies.py` does NOT exist as a standalone file — the install logic is inside `run_all.py`. Remove any reference to it as a standalone file if present.
- Update the repo structure to include the newer files visible in the directory listing that aren't mentioned: `benchmark_compare.py`, `cloud_pipeline.py`, `control_suite.py`, `dag_scheduler.py`, `dataset_normalizer.py`, `experiment_config_loader.py`, `hparam_search.py`, `memory_manager.py`, `multi_seed_runner.py`, `pipeline_critic.py`, `pipeline_types.py`, `plot_convergence.py`, `preflight_checks.py`, `preprocess_seller_split.py`, `resource_optimizer.py`, `startup_diagnostics.py`, `validators.py`, `logging_utils.py`

### 3. `CLAUDE.md` — Sync to latest state

Update these sections in CLAUDE.md:

**§ 6 Repository Structure** — The listed structure shows `paper/` as a subdirectory, but needs to include the many additional file...

</details>

reviews.body:
Brings the benchmark corpus in line with the gallery, which now has 6 showcases (was 4 when the corpus was last authored). Adds two frozen suites and fixes a now-stale README line.

## New suites
- `docs/research/context-benchmark/tasks/keycloak.yaml` — 8 tasks
- `docs/research/context-benchmark/tasks/kafka.yaml` — 8 tasks

Both `yarramate/benchmark-suite/v1`, pinned to the exact commits the gallery models were built against (`73f08b39…` / `26b251a4…`). 4 comprehension (2 foundational + 2 multi-hop) + 2 change + 2 model-maintenance each.

## Multi-hop from the start
Per issue #56 (comprehension saturated at both model tiers in the 2026-07-29 sweep because the original tasks were single-hop), these two suites are built with multi-hop tasks from day one rather than needing a later v2 errata round:
- **Keycloak**: the federated-LDAP credential-check chain (login form → credential-manager dispatch → LDAP storage provider's `CredentialInputValidator` → the actual bind), and the identity-provider-deletion cascade (admin endpoint → `UserProvider#preRemove` → the JPA bulk-delete of federated-identity links, and what does/doesn't happen to the affected local accounts).
- **Kafka**: the `acks=all` acknowledgement path (`DelayedProduce` purgatory operation → `Partition.checkEnoughReplicasReachOffset` → the high-watermark/ISR condition, including the distinct "durably written but not-enough-replicas" error), and classic-protocol consumer-group rebalance (per-consumer offset auto-commit before revoke → broker-elected leader → leader-side `ConsumerPartitionAssignor` invocation).

Model-maintenance tasks extend the workspace into gaps the gallery's own discovery journeys already documented as intentionally out of scope (Keycloak: LDAP sync/import and the authorization-decision path as dynamic views; Kafka: producer idempotence and the transaction coordinator).

## Verification
- `node runner/validate-suite.mjs` passes for both new suites individually and in the full 11-file regression (all existing v1/v2 suites unaffected).
- **Ground truth was independently re-verified** against the pinned clones after drafting (not just trusted from the drafting pass) — this caught and fixed 3 real defects: two off-by-N line-number citations in the Kafka multi-hop tasks (verified via fresh reads against `/tmp/kafka-4.3.1`), and one comprehension prompt that incorrectly implied a method was private when it isn't (`maybeShrinkIsr` is package-visible, not private — the prompt and ground truth now state this explicitly rather than asserting a false premise).
- Every `verifiedAgainst`/`touches` citation passed an automated file-exists + line-in-bounds check, plus manual re-verification of every inline line-number claim in all four comprehension tasks per suite.

## README
Removed the stale "gallery currently provides 4 — add a fifth showcase" corpus warning; it now correctly states all 6 gallery showcases have benchmark suites, clearing the N≥5 headline-pooling threshold from DESIGN.md.

## Process note
The two subagents I originally dispatched to author these in parallel both failed immediately on an account-level `429 Weekly/Monthly Limit Exhausted` (not transient —~73h retry-after), so this was authored solo in the primary session using the exact investigation-and-citation contract I'd written for them, then independently re-verified as above.

Updates `hono` from 4.12.9 to 4.12.12
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Path traversal in toSSG() allows writing files outside the output directory

Affects: toSSG() for Static Site Generation. Fixes a path traversal issue where crafted ssgParams values could write files outside the configured output directory. GHSA-xf4j-xp2r-rqqx

Incorrect IP matching in ipRestriction() for IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses

Affects: IP Restriction Middleware. Fixes improper handling of IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses (e.g. ::ffff:127.0.0.1) that could cause allow/deny rules to be bypassed. GHSA-xpcf-pg52-r92g

Missing validation of cookie name on write path in setCookie()

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Non-breaking space prefix bypass in cookie name handling in getCookie()

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Users who use Serve Static, Static Site Generation, Cookie utilities, or IP restriction middleware are strongly encouraged to upgrade to this version.

Updates `lodash` from 4.17.21 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

reviews.title: Bump the npm_and_yarn group across 1 directory with 10 updates

reviews.body:
Closes #263

Wires resdag's internal fast-path speedups to a committed, CI-gated
performance-regression harness so the headline speed claims can't silently rot.

## What changed

- **`benchmarks/targets.json`** — committed floors per (context, metric) cell.
  - `internal_ratios`: the **hard gate** — hardware-portable CPU A/B ratios
    (resdag's fast path vs its own naive path, no external libraries). Each cell
    carries an `enforced_min_ratio` (gated) and an `aspirational_ratio`
    (audit/GPU headline, documented but not enforced).
  - `external_floors`: **informational only** — cross-library numbers
    transcribed from `benchmarks/results/REPORT.md` (2026-06-14). Never asserted,
    because reservoirpy / ReservoirComputing.jl may be absent.
- **`tests/test_benchmarks/test_perf_regression.py`** — `benchmark`-marked test
  that reads `targets.json` and asserts three internal ratios, each with a
  numerical-correctness check against its naive twin:
  | Ratio | Floor | Ticket |
  |---|---|---|
  | flat forecast vs per-step graph re-execution | ≥ 1.8× | #254 |
  | vectorized NG-RC vs per-step scan | ≥ 5× | #255 |
  | fast spectral radius vs dense eigvals | ≥ 2× | #185 |
  Interleaved best-of-N A/B timing + a small-reservoir config keep the
  flat-engine gate robust on contended runners. A plain (non-benchmark) test
  guards the targets-file shape so the normal lane catches malformed/out-of-sync
  targets.
- **`benchmarks/rc_bench/run.py`** — new `--report` flag renders `REPORT.md` in
  the same deterministic run-and-render step.
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** — benchmark lane now also triggers on the

## What this is

A documentation-only overhaul. I surveyed the full codebase and all active docs, identified what makes Tank World genuinely special, captured a prioritized improvement plan, and fixed documentation that had drifted out of sync with the code. No code changes, no test risk.

## The most interesting aspects (now documented as "crown jewels")

1. **Git as the heredity mechanism** — the `benchmarks/ → champions/ → validate_improvement.py → CI` loop turns "the number went up" into a reproducible scientific claim.
2. **Composable behaviors over black boxes** — fish behavior factors into four orthogonal, genetically-tuned dimensions; interpretable and evolvable.
3. **Determinism as a first-class invariant** — seeded RNG everywhere, record/replay, double-run CI checks.
4. **A full Texas Hold'em engine with CFR learning inside an ALife sim** — fish play poker for energy and inherit learned regret tables.
5. **Multi-world backend** — one evolutionary core renders as fish tank, petri dish, or soccer pitch.

## Changes

**New**
- `docs/IMPROVEMENT_PROPOSALS.md` — a living, prioritized engineering backlog. Names the crown jewels (so we protect them) then gives concrete, effort/impact-tagged implementation plans across five themes: hardening the evolution loop, taming the god files, consolidating the algorithm library, developer/observer experience, and docs that sell the project.
- `docs/archive/README.md` — a retention/deprecation policy so the ~43 archived docs stop sitting beside active ones without context.

**README**
- Added CI / benchmark / Python / license / black badges.
- Replaced the ASCII evolution-loop and three-layer descriptions with rendered **Mermaid diagrams** (hardened to avoid `&` in labels for cross-renderer safety).

- `scripts/README.md`: expanded from a partial list to a grouped reference of the evolution-loop, analysis, diagnosis, profiling, and verification scripts (every entry verified to exist).

v4.12.12

Security fixes

This release includes fixes for the following security issues:

Middleware bypass via repeated slashes in serveStatic

Affects: Serve Static middleware. Fixes a path normalization inconsistency where repeated slashes (//) could bypass route-based middleware protections and allow access to protected static files. GHSA-wmmm-f939-6g9c

Affects: setCookie(), serialize(), and serializeSigned() from hono/cookie. Fixes missing validation of cookie names on the write path, preventing inconsistent handling between parsing and serialization. GHSA-26pp-8wgv-hjvm

Affects: getCookie() from hono/cookie. Fixes a discrepancy in cookie name handling that could allow attacker-controlled cookies to override legitimate ones and bypass prefix protections. GHSA-r5rp-j6wh-rvv4

Updates `lodash-es` from 4.17.23 to 4.18.1
Release notes

Sourced from lodash-es's releases.

4.18.1

Bugs

Fixes a ReferenceError issue in lodash lodash-es lodash-amd and lodash.template when using the template and fromPairs functions from the modular builds. See lodash/lodash#6167

These defects were related to how lodash distributions are built from the main branch using https://github.com/lodash-archive/lodash-cli. When internal dependencies change inside lodash functions, equivalent updates need to be made to a mapping in the lodash-cli. (hey, it was ahead of its time once upon a time!). We know this, but we missed it in the last release. It's the kind of thing that passes in CI, but fails bc the build is not the same thing you tested.

There is no diff on main for this, but you can see the diffs for each of the npm packages on their respective branches:

  • lodash: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm...4.18.1-npm
  • lodash-es: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-es...4.18.1-es
  • lodash-amd: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-amd...4.18.1-amd
  • lodash.templatehttps://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.18.0-npm-packages...4.18.1-npm-packages

4.18.0

v4.18.0

Full Changelog: https://github.com/lodash/lodash/compare/4.17.23...4.18.0

Security

_.unset / _.omit: Fixed prototype pollution via constructor/prototype path traversal (GHSA-f23m-r3pf-42rh, fe8d32e). Previously, array-wrapped path segments and primitive roots could bypass the existing guards, allowing deletion of properties from built-in prototypes. Now constructor and prototype are blocked unconditionally as non-terminal path keys, matching baseSet. Calls that previously returned true and deleted the property now return false and leave the target untouched.

_.template: Fixed code injection via imports keys (GHSA-r5fr-rjxr-66jc, CVE-2026-4800, 879aaa9). Fixes an incomplete patch for CVE-2021-23337. The variable option was validated against reForbiddenIdentifierChars but importsKeys was left unguarded, allowing code injection via the same Function() constructor sink. imports keys containing forbidden identifier characters now throw "Invalid imports option passed into _.template".

Docs

  • Add security notice for _.template in threat model and API docs (#6099)
  • Document lower > upper behavior in _.random (#6115)
  • Fix quotes in _.compact jsdoc (#6090)

lodash.* modular packages

Diff

We have also regenerated and published a select number of the lodash.* modular packages.

These modular packages had fallen out of sync significantly from the minor/patch updates to lodash. Specifically, we have brought the following packages up to parity w/ the latest lodash release because they have had CVEs on them in the past:

v8.4.2

Performance

https://github.com/pillarjs/path-to-regexp/compare/v8.4.1...v8.4.2

v8.4.1

Fixed

  • Remove trie deduplication (#431) 6bc8e84
    • Using a trie required non-greedy matching, which regressed wildcards in non-ending mode by matching them up until the first match. For example:
      • /*foo with /a/b = /a
      • /*foo.htmlwith /a/b.html/c.html = /a/b.html
  • Allow backtrack handling to match itself (#427) 5bcd30b
    • When backtracking was introduced, it rejected matching things like /:"a"_:"b" against /foo__. This makes intuitive sense because the second parameter is not going to backtrack on _ anymore, but it's somewhat unexpected since there's no reason it shouldn't match the second _.

reviews.body:
# PR: Reverse audit — state-to-context verification after compaction

## Blind spot addressed

MemLock's forward audit (`audit_anchors` / `semantic_audit_anchors`) starts
from configured/pinned anchors and asks "did this anchor survive
compaction?". A stored user preference that was never configured as an
anchor is invisible to it. The regression test
`test_forward_only_blind_spot_passes_while_reverse_audit_finds_dependency`
proves the gap: with no anchors configured, forward verification reports
zero drift (`alive_ids=[], drifted_ids=[]`) while `reverse_audit()` finds
the stored material preference `ABSENT` and flags it as a rehydration
candidate.

`reverse_audit()` closes this by starting from **every stored preference**
and asking "is this preference still supported by the active
post-compaction context?".

## What shipped

- `detection.py`: pure, deterministic `reverse_audit(memories, active_region,
  *, now, drift_threshold)` + `reverse_audit_unavailable()` fail-open report.
  Verdicts: `PRESENT / ABSENT / CONTRADICTED / STORED_STALE / AMBIGUOUS /
  UNKNOWN`; structured findings with IDs, evidence, reasons, actions;
  `rehydrate_ids` and `suppressed_ids` lists.
- `__init__.py`: post-compaction reverse pass via a host-supplied preference
  provider (`set_reverse_preference_provider`); `ABSENT + material`
  rehydration candidates merge into the existing priority/slot/char budget;
  provider failure fails open and leaves the turn unchanged.
- `store.py`: optional `reverse` diagnostics on `drift_log` entries.
- `persistence.py`: mnemosyne backend now explicitly raises
  `BackendUnavailableError` instead of silently falling back to FileStore.
- `config.yaml` / `plugin.yaml`: `reverse_audit: false` (disabled by
  default), `reverse_preference_query`, `reverse_limit`; version 0.3.0.
- `docs/REVERSE_AUDIT.md` (new): usage, report interpretation, Mnemosyne
  failure behaviour, forward-vs-reverse distinction, unsupported forms.
  README/ARCHITECTURE/DESIGN updated.
- Tests: `tests/test_reverse_audit_unit.py` (implementation unit tests,
  incl. pre_llm integration + provider-failure), `tests/test_reverse_audit.py`
  + `tests/fixtures/reverse_audit_stale.json` (STALE benchmark suite).

## Contract reconciliation (from t_87076251's 3-pass/5-mismatch report)

1. **Contradiction semantics** — impl now honours
   `metadata.memlock.{preference_key,value}` on active user messages
   (contract §5), not only `key: value` text syntax. Fixture case
   `contradicted-current-context` now returns `CONTRADICTED/suppress`.
2. **Superseded wording** — reason unified to `"stored preference is
   superseded"`, evidence `["superseded_by=<id>"]` (contract §94);
   `STORED_STALE` findings preserve explicit materiality.
3. **ABSENT wording** — unified to the contract-stable
   `"no supporting or contradicting evidence in active context"`.
4. **Error key** — query-failure errors use `reason` consistently across
   the pure function, the boundary harness and the fixture (was split

reviews.body:
The Benchmarks workflow crashed on the v1.5.0 release ([run 31267507913](https://github.com/jeremydaly/lambda-api/actions/runs/31267507913)):

```
Error: Cannot find module '/home/runner/work/lambda-api/lambda-api/dist/cjs/index.js'.
Please verify that the package.json has a valid "main" entry
    at Object.<anonymous> (benchmarks/frameworks/lambda-api.js:10:19)
```

## Root cause

`benchmarks/frameworks/lambda-api.js` loads the library from the working tree with `require('../../')`, which resolves through the root package's `main`. #326 changed `main` from `index.js` to `./dist/cjs/index.js`, so the adapter now requires a build — but the workflow only ran `npm ci` inside `benchmarks/`, never installing or building the root package.

The benchmark suite (#327) merged before the dual build (#326), and benchmarks only run on `release: published`, so v1.5.0 was the first time the two met. The `baseline` framework has no lambda-api dependency and completed fine, which is why the log shows 10 green scenarios before the crash.

## Fixes

**1. Build `dist/` before benchmarking.** Adds a root `npm ci --ignore-scripts` + `npm run build` ahead of the benchmark install, matching how `release.yml` sequences the same steps.

**2. Honor `LAMBDA_API_VERSION` in the adapter.** Surfaced while verifying the first fix. `run.js:65` already read the env var, but only for the run metadata that renders the caption — the per-framework table rows use each adapter's own `version` field, and lambda-api's read `package.json` directly. Since that ships a `0.0.0-development` placeholder until publish time, every table row would have rendered as:

```
| lambda-api `0.0.0-development` | 298,049 | ...
```

while the caption directly above it correctly said `lambda-api v1.5.0`. That would have been committed straight into the README by the workflow's final step. The adapter now uses the same `LAMBDA_API_VERSION || pkg.version` precedence as `run.js`.

## Verification

Reproduced locally by deleting `dist/` — same `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` at the same adapter line; loads cleanly after `npm run build`.

Ran the exact workflow command end-to-end (`node run.js --md results/RESULTS.md --json results/raw.json --update-readme` with `LAMBDA_API_VERSION=1.5.0`). All 6 frameworks × 10 scenarios complete, and both the caption and every table row now read `1.5.0`. Generated results were reverted out of this branch — the committed numbers should come from the runner, not my laptop.

The subsequent `Format README` step pins `prettier@2`, which matches the repo's `^2.3.2` devDependency, so no version skew there.

## Note

The v1.5.0 README still has stale benchmark numbers, since the workflow never reached its commit step. Once this merges, re-running the workflow via `workflow_dispatch` with version `1.5.0` will refresh it.

## Summary
- Retires ASV's whole per-commit tracking machinery — commit-by-commit performance tracking for CrocoDash/mom6_forge now lives in those repos' own pytest-benchmark suites instead.
- SeaSloth keeps only stable-reference, one-time benchmarks that don't change per commit: xESMF/ESMF regridding, the mom6_forge bathymetry pipeline, and the CrocoDash OBC regrid+merge pipeline. Runoff mapping and import-time benchmarks move out (out of scope here).
- Every ASV `bench_*.py` class becomes a plain pytest `test_*.py` function using the `benchmark` fixture (`benchmark()` or `benchmark.pedantic()` for expensive/data-dependent cases); `pytest.mark.skipif` replaces `setup()`'s `NotImplementedError` for missing data.
- New `pytest.mark.light`/`heavy`: the smallest synthetic xESMF/ESMF combo is a fast smoke test (`pytest -m light`); `test_topo.py`/`test_obc.py` are always `heavy` since even their smallest size needs real GEBCO/GLORYS data.
- Report generation dramatically simplified: two plain-table HTML pages (`report/index.html`, `report/health.html`), no matplotlib charts, no hand-written narrative.
- Data access health stays a separate daily-run script/page (`check_data_access.py` → `results/health.json` → `generate_health_report.py`), independent of the on-demand perf benchmarks.
- CI collapses to one workflow (manual dispatch + daily schedule) that only rebuilds both pages from committed `results/*.json` and deploys to Pages.

## What & why

Follow-up to #2158 (design brief, merged). E1 — the premise test the design doc staged first — **ran**, and it overturned our proudest number honestly.

### E1 result (`data/sigma0/e1_degloss_report.json`, MEASURED)
De-gloss the 66 held-out golden statements (strip in-text status stamps like "— OPEN"/"— REFUTED"; keep canonical names), re-run the **same** adapter in-process:

| held-out 66 | golden | confab (negatives asserted) | over-abstention |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ouro — original | 0.958 | 2/20 · **10%** | 2.2% |
| **Ouro — de-glossed** | 0.833 | 11/20 · **55%** | 0.0% |
| GPT-4o-mini — control | 0.964→0.976 | **0/20 → 0/20** | — |

The GPT-4o-mini control is unmoved, so de-gloss does **not** make the task harder — Ouro's 5.5× confab spike is the tune **reading glosses, not honesty**. The "10% confab / ties GPT-4o-mini" headline is **retracted** (frontier-brief thesis + model-design doc + benchmark table corrected in this PR).

### Corpus-v2 (D2) — fixes the leak at the source
- **De-gloss at emit time**: status lives ONLY in the answer key; a de-gloss **lint** (`_leaks`) enforces it so the leak can't silently return (canonical names + math words like "open interval" survive).
- **Anti-shortcut families a gloss-reader can't game**: 21 **perturbed-positives** (true theorems mutated false), 12 **fictional** items (nonexistent → must ABSTAIN), plus contested measurements + more open/refuted for family coverage.
- **204 items, 87 negatives (42.6%, inside the 0.40–0.55 gate)**, all 6 status families present, sha256-stratified LOSO holdout.
- **Frozen v1 SEED untouched** — its web-validation test still passes.

### Tests
`tests/test_corpus_v2_degloss.py` (9) + v1 web-validation (8) = **17/17 green**.

### Staged (NOT faked)
Scaling to the ~600-item / ≥100-held-out-negative **web-validated** target needs the 3-validator pipeline — deliberately not fabricated here. That web-validation pass + the E4 retrain-on-corpus-v2 + OSS-mark eval (TruthfulQA / HaluEval / AbstentionBench) produce the first *defensible* honesty number.
