Fixes the CodeRabbit review findings raised against the **vendored** copy of this skill in
[ponderousdev/ponderous-site#31](https://github.com/ponderousdev/ponderous-site/pull/31) (plus 3 from
[ponderousdev/lawnomator-site#14](https://github.com/ponderousdev/lawnomator-site/pull/14)). Downstream
copies are drift-checked and never edited, so every accepted finding is fixed here in the canonical
source (`ai/skills/frontend/design-handoff/`); consumers pick it up on the next skill sync.

## Verdicts — ponderous-site#31

| Finding (comment id) | File | Verdict | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tall pages truncated to top slice (3566278381) | `assets/brand-screenshots.spec.ts` | **Accepted** | Pages over the capture cap are now captured as stacked `-part1/-part2/…` clips (`fullPage` + document-relative `clip`) covering through the bottom; in-cap pages keep the single fullPage file. |
| Overflow guard light-theme-only (3566278384) | `assets/brand-screenshots.spec.ts` | **Accepted** | Guard now runs per route × theme via the existing `setTheme` helper. |
| Alpha dropped before contrast scoring (3566278387) | `assets/check-contrast.mjs` | **Accepted** | Alpha preserved for oklch/hex(#rrggbbaa)/rgb[a]; translucent fg composited over the audited bg (gamma sRGB) before scoring; translucent bg reported unsupported → rendered check, never PASS on the opaque value. Verified against an alpha fixture (a 0.35-alpha `muted-foreground` that passed before now FAILs). |
| Inline-style bypasses: gradient literals, hsla(), color() (3566278389) | `assets/check-off-palette.sh` | **Accepted** | Attribute pattern scans the whole style value (bounded at quote/semicolon), both patterns flag rgba/hsla/hwb/lab/lch/`color()`; `background-image`/`outline-color`/`caret-color` added. Regression-run: 10 bypass cases flagged, 6 `var(--token)` negatives clean. (No asset-test harness exists in this repo; cases documented in the commit.) |
| Bogus ratios over painted backgrounds (3566278394) | `assets/measure-rendered-contrast.mjs` | **Accepted** | Samples over a `background-image` or painted `::before`/`::after` anywhere in the ancestor chain now fail as `UNSUPPORTED` (fail-closed) with a manual-measurement instruction; overlay siblings are documented as undetectable/manual-only. |
| **Critical: shell interpolation in `ingest:design`** (3566278397) | `assets/Taskfile.design.yml` | **Accepted** | `BUNDLE`/`DEST` now pass via Task `env:` (never spliced into shell source) to a new `assets/ingest-design.sh`, which picks tar vs unzip by validated extension. Tested: `BUNDLE='x.tar.gz; touch PWNED'` does not execute; paths with spaces work. |
| Document unsupported painted backgrounds (3566278401) | `references/accessibility-verification.md` | **Accepted** | New "What it can't model" bullet: UNSUPPORTED samples and overlay siblings require manual/pixel measurement; no sample accepted without a measured number. |
| `@font-face` before `@import "tailwindcss"` kills the import (3566278404) | `references/assets-fonts-favicons.md` | **Accepted** | Example reordered (imports first); the incorrect "`@font-face` blocks can go anywhere" claim rewritten — any rule before an `@import` invalidates it. |
| Email contract contradiction (3566278408) | `references/brand-page.md` | **Accepted** | One workflow now: hand-built table-HTML (the zero-dependency pattern) is the documented email path; React Email only if the repo already carries the dependency. |
| PDFs overclaimed as print-ready (3566278410) | `references/brand-page.md` | **Accepted** (prose fix, not machinery) | Recipe outputs labeled **digital-proof PDFs** (RGB, bleed size, no crop marks); Tier 3 Print states true print-ready output needs a dedicated production export + vendor validation. |
| Bootstrap truncates existing stylesheet (3566278412) | `references/greenfield-bootstrap.md` | **Accepted** | Rule is now create-empty **only if absent**; existing (token-less) `globals.css` contents are preserved, with a recoverability note for untracked files. |
| Zip-slip on bundle extraction (3566278413) | `references/ingesting-the-bundle.md` | **Accepted** | Archive treated as untrusted: `ingest-design.sh` rejects absolute paths, `..` traversal, and link entries before extracting (tested against crafted tar/zip archives); manual grep equivalent documented. |
| Dev-server contradiction (3566278415) | `references/responsive-and-cross-browser.md` | **Accepted** | The stray "point them at the dev server" line now says production `build && preview`, matching the config and the spec header. |
| `sidebar-*` claimed theme-constant by convention (3566278418) | `references/token-reconciliation.md` | **Accepted** | Corrected: shadcn writes *different* sidebar values in `:root` vs `.dark`; constant chrome requires deleting/aligning the `.dark` overrides — or dedicated fixed-chrome tokens when a real themed sidebar coexists. |
| `.zip` handoff contract mismatch (3566278420) | `SKILL.md` + `references/ingesting-the-bundle.md` | **Accepted** | Both docs now agree: identify the coding handoff by **content shape** (README + `chats/` + project), never extension; the raw-assets "Download as .zip" export lacks that shape and is rejected. Extraction flow (`ingest:design`) accepts both `.tar.gz` and `.zip` after entry validation. |

## Verdicts — lawnomator-site#14

| Finding (comment id) | File | Verdict | Resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attribute` regex misses `rgba(`/`hsla(` (3566249742) | `assets/check-off-palette.sh` | **Accepted** | Folded into the shared `rgba?\(`/`hsla?\(` color-function alternation used by both patterns. |
| `2>/dev/null` masks a bad `$root` as "clean" (3566249745) | `assets/check-off-palette.sh` | **Accepted** | Missing target dir now exits 2 with an error instead of reporting the gate clean. |

**Rejected:** none — every finding reproduced against the canonical source.

## Notes

reviews.body:
## Summary

Authors the two documents the build prompt treats as the contract for this project. Neither existed: the
repository had no commits, no default branch, and no specification. Every issue after this one was blocked on
it, so this pull request is the cheapest point at which the contract can be corrected.

`README.md` is the technical specification, seventeen numbered sections with the canonical results table at
section 13 as the build prompt requires. `BREAKDOWN.md` is the execution plan, thirty-nine issues across six
milestones with branch names, dependencies, reviewable-line budgets, and the ordering constraints that are not
negotiable.

## What changed

- `README.md`, new. Principles as testable properties; a Mermaid system diagram and a Mermaid triage sequence
  diagram with boundary boxes for the agent workflow and the evaluation plane; repository structure; model
  backends with pinned identifiers and the cost formula; event sources and the normalized envelope; the three
  hop schemas; the three mechanical grounding checks; the two scoreboards including the judge audit; the
  escalation policy as versioned configuration; replay determinism and its limits; observability; security and
  untrusted input; the results table; milestones; run targets; the development process; the definition of done.
- `BREAKDOWN.md`, new. Thirty-nine issues, six milestone tables, five non-negotiable ordering constraints, and
  the three categories of change that require an owner conversation before they are made.
- `.gitignore`, in the preceding bootstrap commit on the default branch.

Three decisions are recorded in the specification because they are load-bearing and expensive to reverse:
pgvector inside PostgreSQL rather than a separate vector service, Kafka in KRaft mode with a single broker, and
a prose linter in continuous integration from M0. The measurements behind all three are in a commit comment on
24fc976.

## How it was validated

The prose constraints are mechanically checkable, so they were checked mechanically rather than by reading:

```
grep -nP '[\x{2014}\x{2013}]' README.md BREAKDOWN.md          # em and en dashes: none
grep -nEi "\b(can't|won't|don't|it's|that's|...)\b" ...        # contractions: none
grep -nE "TODO|FIXME|TBD|XXX|placeholder" ...                  # placeholders: none
grep -nE "\ban [bcdfgjklmnpqrstvwxyz]" ...                     # article errors: one found
```

The last check caught an incorrect indefinite article at `README.md:320` that two readings had missed. It is
fixed in this branch, and it is the argument for issue 4 landing the same check in continuous integration
rather than relying on review.

Section counts, the position of the results table at section 13, and the issue count of thirty-nine against
the definition-of-done floor of thirty were verified by hand against the build prompt.

## Risks and follow-ups

**The specification encodes an interpretation.** It was authored from the build prompt because the named
contract files did not exist anywhere: not in the working tree, not on the remote, and not in the owner's home
directory or across the other thirty repositories on the account. If any section misreads intent, correcting it
here costs one pull request; correcting it after thirty-eight issues are open costs considerably more.

**Section 10 narrows a hard rule rather than satisfying it.** Hard rule 6 asks for replay determinism. The
pinned model rejects `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`, so byte-identical replay is not achievable and
claiming it would put a false statement in the contract. The specification instead defines determinism as an
identical event sequence, an identical pinned corpus and index, and identical prompts, schemas, policy, and
model identifier, with output variance measured across three runs per scored configuration and reported as a
mean with a range. A reported delta falling inside that range is visibly not a result. This is the one place
where the specification does not simply restate the build prompt, and it is the section most worth reviewing.

**M1 blocks a model credential.** Hard rule 1 forbids agent code until the judge harness runs and the
scoreboard prints, and the judge requires a model. There is no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment and no
local inference runtime installed. M0 is unaffected; issue 13 cannot complete without the key.

**Follow-ups already scheduled rather than left implicit:** the prose linter is issue 4, the kind, kubectl, and
helm installs are issue 5, and the Mermaid-to-HTML synchronization check is issue 6.

## Reviewer notes

Read specification section 10 first. It is the only section that narrows a stated hard rule, and if the
narrowing is wrong then the comparison methodology for every experiment in M2 through M5 is wrong with it.

Second, `BREAKDOWN.md` ordering constraint 1: issue 14 before issue 20, the scoreboard printing before the
first agent exists. That is hard rule 1, it is the constraint most likely to be violated under time pressure,
and it is checkable at review time by confirming nothing under `anomalydesk/agents/` appears before issue 14 is
merged.

Third, the pinned models and rates in section 4. Both agents and judge are pinned to `claude-opus-5` at 5.00
and 25.00 per million input and output tokens. Rates are written in exactly one place and the ledger stores
tokens rather than money, so a price change does not require reprocessing history.

Closes #1

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change | OpenSSF |
|---|---|---|---|---|

#### Details
##### Impact
The CIRCL implementation of FourQ fails to validate user-supplied low-order points during Diffie-Hellman key exchange, potentially allowing attackers to force the identity point and compromise session security.

Moreover, there is an incorrect point validation in ScalarMult can lead to incorrect results in the isEqual function and if a point is on the curve.

##### Patches
Version 1.6.1 (https://github.com/cloudflare/circl/tree/v1.6.1) mitigates the identified issues.

We acknowledge Alon Livne (Botanica Software Labs) for the reported findings.

reviews.title: chore(deps): update module github.com/cloudflare/circl to v1.6.1 [security] (release-0.34)

reviews.body: **TL;DR** — A Tossing Room bin now holds **at most one item**, and each bin has **its own emptying button beside it**. That is the whole fix for the scoring defect [#73](https://github.com/joshnroy/human-in-the-loop-practice-makes-perfect/pull/73) diagnosed: `ItemInBin` is `Throw`'s add-effect but reads the *bin's* count, so a throw into an already-occupied bin was scored a success at any force. With capacity 1 and `BinEmpty` as `Throw`'s precondition, the count is provably 0 at throw time, so `ItemInBin` flips false → true **exactly once per throw** — no `in_bin` flag, no counting predicates. Measured over 10 seeds × 2500 practice transitions, the trash binding of `Throw`: **main scored 435 successes against 174 that landed (261/435 were misses)**; this branch scores **265 against 265 landed, 0/265 inflated**. Recycling: **0/83** and **0/52**. The asymmetry survives — recycling is attempted at most once per period in **250/250** periods. The oracle solves all three families, EMPTY included, **300/300 each**, and EES's planner solves the newly-ordered EMPTY **200/200** unpracticed. Because this changes *dynamics*, prior Tossing Room results are **not re-scorable — they are incomparable**; the list is below and it is longer than #73's. ## Question / goal Close the `Throw`-scoring defect by making the domain's representation honest rather than by bolting a second feature onto it, and report exactly which published Tossing Room numbers that invalidates. #73's diagnosis, measurements and blast-radius table are the starting point and are cited rather than re-derived — but #73's central framing ("mis-scored, therefore re-scorable") does not survive a change to dynamics, and correcting that is half the job. ## Background Tossing Room is a 1-D hallway of rooms. A robot sorts items from a limitless pile at its start room (3) into a recycling bin (room 1) and a trash bin (room 6). A **one-way ledge** between rooms 2 and 3 can be crossed leftward but never rightward — the domain's single irreversible action — so the recycling bin is reachable exactly once per period, and never again. `Throw` is the only stochastic skill: it lands only in the item's own bin room and only when the sampled force is within `throw_tolerance` of that item's target. **A throw always releases the item, hit or miss** — itself an earlier fix, because a miss that changed nothing let the robot re-throw for free and quietly turned the evaluation horizon into an "attempts" dial. EES scores a skill execution by `add_effects ⊆ atoms(next_state)` (`ees_method.py`, `observe_pending`), and that verdict feeds two things: the per-ground-skill competence model, and the label on the sampler's training row. `Throw`'s add-effect is `ItemInBin(item, bin)`, classified as `count >= 1 and item_kind == bin_kind` — **a property of the bin, not of the throw**. So the defect is a granularity mismatch, not a coding error: a predicate that is defensible as a *goal* ("the bin holds trash") is wrong as an *effect* ("this throw put trash in the bin"). Two things made a bin non-empty during practice: EMPTY-goal tasks prefilled both bins with 1–3 items, and within a period the first landed throw made every subsequent throw of that kind free. Only trash could exploit the second, because the ledge severs the recycling bin from the pile. Previously there was also **one** "empty/incinerate" button, in room 6, which emptied **both** bins at once. That is why `Press` carried `ignore_effects={ItemInBin}`: emptying both bins falsifies every `ItemInBin` atom, a universal delete no per-item `delete_effect` could express for an operator with no item parameter. `ignore_effects` was the blunt instrument that bought correctness at the price of also telling the planner that emptying one bin empties the other. **The mechanism this PR introduces.** `BIN_CAPACITY = 1`. `_apply_throw` *refuses* a throw at a full bin — a silent no-op, the same totality convention every out-of-context action here follows — and `Throw` gains the matching `BinEmpty(?bin)` precondition, so the symbolic model is exactly as strong as the guard. A refusal is not a miss: nothing is consumed, so this does not reopen the free re-roll that releasing the item closed; emptying the bin first costs a `Press` the planner has to schedule. With `BinEmpty` holding at throw time the count is 0, so a landed throw takes `ItemInBin` from false to true and a miss leaves it false. That is the entire fix. `ItemInBin` stays count-based and there is deliberately **no `in_bin` feature**: `count ∈ {0, 1}` is already exactly the bit both `ItemInBin` and `BinEmpty` need, and storing the same fact twice is the shape this redesign exists to avoid. ## Hypothesis 1. Capacity 1 plus a `BinEmpty` precondition makes the vacuous success **unreachable by construction**, so post-fix the EES-scored and actually-landed counts must be *identical* per binding. Any gap means the vacuity survived. 2. The domain's defining asymmetry must survive: trash stays retryable within a practice period (throw → press → walk to pile → pickup → walk back → throw, ~9 steps against 8 today, so roughly 11 attempts per 100-step period instead of 12), and recycling stays attemptable exactly once ever, because the ledge severs its bin from the pile. 3. EMPTY becomes an **ordering task** — both buttons must be pressed and the recycling one is behind the ledge, so trash-first is the only solution and the reverse order is unsolvable. This is accepted deliberately: it makes EMPTY exercise the irreversibility the domain is about rather than being a deterministic smoke test. 4. `Press` per bin should make `ignore_effects` unnecessary rather than merely smaller. ## Guidance given - Supersede #73. **Do not cherry-pick its code** — it added an `in_bin` flag, which this design makes unnecessary. Read its description first and cite its diagnosis rather than re-deriving it. - Keep `ItemInBin` count-based; one responsibility per feature. - Tie button ↔ bin symbolically so `Press`'s effect is expressible, and **check whether `ignore_effects` is still needed** once effects are per-bin; remove it if not. - The invariant "the model is exactly as strong as `_apply_throw`'s guard" is stated repeatedly in this domain's docstrings and walked by `tests/environments/test_operator_dynamics_fidelity.py` — keep it true. - **Measure**, don't assume: per-throw-binding attempts / scored / landed over 10 seeds, per-period attempt counts for both bindings, oracle solve rates per family as x/y. If recycling is ever attempted twice, something is wrong. If the oracle cannot solve the new EMPTY, say so loudly rather than weakening the task. - Report what this invalidates as carefully as the fix. Do not silently edit merged logs. #73's table is a starting point but its "re-scorable" framing no longer applies — say so. - Counts as x/y, never bare percentages. Do not touch `environments/tossingroomsplit/` or PRs #70/#71. ## Methods ### The design, and the two things it deliberately does not do **No `in_bin` flag (#73's approach).** #73 chose it for a real reason — the singleton discriminator objects `trash`/`recycling` denote *the item in play*, so "is it in its bin" reads as a property of that item. But it stores the bin's contents twice, in two features that must be kept in agreement by three separate dynamics branches, and it required `Pickup` to grow a `?bin` parameter purely to declare a delete effect on a flag it clears. Capacity 1 gets the same guarantee from the representation that already exists: with `count ∈ {0, 1}` and `Throw` requiring `BinEmpty`, the count *is* the flag, and `Pickup` needs no change at all. **No comparing counts across the transition.** Rejected in #73 for a reason that still holds: `observe_pending` is handed only `true_atoms=abstract_state(next_state)`, so threading a previous state in changes `core/`'s `Method` contract for every domain, and a delta-based classifier stops being a function of a single `State` — which `Goal.is_satisfied`, `SkillGrounder.abstract_state` and PDDL initial-state rendering all require. **Keeping the model exactly as strong as the dynamics.** `Throw` gains `BinEmpty(?bin)` as a precondition **and as a delete effect**. The delete matters as much as the precondition: without it the planner believes it can throw a second item into the same bin, which is the same model-above-reality shape as this domain's three previously-shipped defects. `Press` becomes `(?robot, ?button, ?room, ?bin, ?item)` with `ButtonForBin(?button, ?bin)` pinning the bin to the pressed button and `BinAcceptsItem(?item, ?bin)` pinning the item to that bin — one valid grounding per button, not a widening. `ItemInBin(?item, ?bin)` is then an ordinary `delete_effect`, and **`ignore_effects` is removed entirely**: with per-bin buttons, a mismatched-kind `ItemInBin` is false in every state, so the named delete is the only atom a press can falsify. `Press`'s raw-action `arg`, previously unused, now names which button — so the pressed button is carried by the action rather than inferred from position, which stays unambiguous under any layout. **A button per bin, beside its bin.** There is no `--button-room` flag and no `button_room` config any more: a button sits in its bin's room by construction (`button_room_for_kind`), because two knobs that must agree is a footgun and "beside its bin" is structural. `button_type` gains a `kind` feature, the exact parallel of how a bin's kind ties it to the item it accepts. **Prefill and horizon.** EMPTY prefills exactly 1 per bin (`initial_count_low`/`initial_count_high` are gone — a bin has one legal non-empty value left), and `build_initial_state` *raises* rather than clamps on a count above capacity, since accepting it would put the environment in a state `Throw`'s precondition assumes away. `longest_shortest_solve` now costs EMPTY as a walk-press-walk-press over both orders, taking the cheaper feasible one, so the default layout's horizon moves **7 → 12**. ### The measurement Two throwaway instrumented harnesses (not committed — `analysis/` is post-run-only), each run against both arms: this branch, and a clean `git archive` of `main` at `d9ddff4`, under an identical protocol. **Pairing correction, worth stating.** The obvious instrumentation — a FIFO pairing `_apply_throw` calls to `EesMethod.observe_outcome` calls — **silently desynchronises**, because EES leaves the last skill of every period unobserved by design (this class's deviation 2). My first run showed a spurious 15/260 gap from exactly that drift. The reported figures instead compute EES's own verdict (`add_effects ⊆ atoms(next_state)` for the grounding the preconditions force) at the throw itself, which is what `observe_pending` evaluates one step later with no intervening action. The unpaired aggregate confirms it: EES recorded 554 `Throw` outcomes against 558 attempts, and 263 successes against my 265 — the difference being exactly the unobserved final skills. Protocol: `--env tossingroom --method ees --num-test-tasks 30 --max-steps-per-interaction 100`, 10 seeds, at both `--num-cycles 5` (500 practice transitions, the briefed budget) and `--num-cycles 25` (2500, for statistical power). ## Results ### Practice-time `Throw` attempts, scored vs landed, 10 seeds pooled **500 practice transitions per seed:** | binding | arm | attempts | EES-scored successes | actually landed | scored successes that were misses | attempts into an occupied bin | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `Throw(…, trash_bin, …)` | **main** | 155 | 71 | 25 | **46/71** | 49/155 | | `Throw(…, trash_bin, …)` | **this PR** | 140 | 37 | 37 | **0/37** | **0/140** | | `Throw(…, recycling_bin, …)` | **main** | 38 | 3 | 3 | **0/3** | 0/38 | | `Throw(…, recycling_bin, …)` | **this PR** | 31 | 4 | 4 | **0/4** | 0/31 | **2500 practice transitions per seed:** | binding | arm | attempts | EES-scored successes | actually landed | scored successes that were misses | attempts into an occupied bin | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | `Throw(…, trash_bin, …)` | **main** | 654 | 435 | 174 | **261/435** | 323/654 | | `Throw(…, trash_bin, …)` | **this PR** | 558 | 265 | 265 | **0/265** | **0/558** | | `Throw(…, recycling_bin, …)` | **main** | 213 | 83 | 83 | **0/83** | 0/213 | | `Throw(…, recycling_bin, …)` | **this PR** | 169 | 52 | 52 | **0/52** | 0/169 | Scored and landed are **identical in every cell of this branch**, both bindings, both budgets, and no throw ever reaches an occupied bin (`0/558`, `0/169`) — the state that made the vacuous success possible is unreachable, not merely unlikely. The predicted asymmetry reproduces on `main` at the larger budget: the trash grounding's competence model was fed 435/654 successes against a true 174/654, while the recycling grounding's was fed 83/83 against a true 83/83 — two separately-keyed models corrupted at wildly different rates, feeding one pooled sampler classifier. **Against #73's numbers.** #73 reported 277 trash attempts / 154 scored / 45 landed / 109-of-154 inflated, and 34/4/4/0 for recycling. The *shape* reproduces exactly (trash inflated, recycling not at all) but the absolute counts do not, and I could not reproduce its harness: its stated protocol at the default `--max-steps-per-interaction 150` yields far fewer throws per seed on `main` than its table shows. I report my own two-arm measurement under one protocol rather than reconciling to a number I cannot regenerate; **treat #73's absolute counts as unverified**. ### Attempts per 100-step practice period Measured two ways. First, what EES actually did (it spends most of a period on `MoveRoom`, so this is a realised rate, not a capacity): | binding | arm | mean attempts/period | max in one period | periods with ≥2 attempts | |---|---|---|---|---| | trash | main | 2.62 | 12 | 74/250 | | trash | this PR | 2.28 | 12 | 64/245 | | recycling | main | 0.85 | **1** | **0/250** | | recycling | this PR | 0.69 | **1** | **0/245** | Second, the structural retry cost — a policy that does nothing but retry, 10 seeds: | binding | arm | policy | attempts per period | |---|---|---|---| | trash | main (optimal: never presses, a full bin still accepts) | random force | **12** in 10/10 seeds | | trash | this PR | random force (~19% hit rate) | **12** in 10/10 seeds | | trash | main | every throw lands | **12** in 10/10 seeds | | trash | this PR | every throw lands (worst case: a `Press` before every retry) | **11** in 10/10 seeds | | recycling | both arms, all four policies | — | **1** in 10/10 seeds | **The asymmetry survives, and the predicted 12 → 11 is a worst case rather than the typical one.** A retry costs 9 steps instead of 8 only when the previous throw *landed*, since only then is a `Press` needed. At the ~19% hit rate a random-force policy actually sees, a period contains ~3 landings and the 3 spare steps absorb them, so 12 attempts still fit; the cost bites at ≥4 landings. Under a perfect thrower every retry pays the `Press` and it is 11, exactly as predicted. **Recycling was never attempted twice: 0/250 and 0/245 periods across the EES runs, and exactly 1 under a dedicated retry loop in 10/10 seeds.** ### The oracle, and the newly-ordered EMPTY | goal family | privileged skill-oracle, 10 seeds × 30 test tasks | EES planner (real Fast Downward), **unpracticed**, 10 seeds × 20 tasks | |---|---|---| | TRASH | **300/300** (30/30 in every seed) | 35/200 | | RECYCLING | **300/300** (30/30 in every seed) | 48/200 | | EMPTY | **300/300** (30/30 in every seed) | **200/200** | | mixed 14/14/2 | **300/300** | — | The oracle solves all three families, EMPTY included, and `test_oracle_presses_both_buttons_in_the_only_feasible_order` asserts the realised action sequence is `[TRASH_KIND, RECYCLING_KIND]` — not merely that it solved. Fast Downward finds the ordered two-press plan unaided in 200/200 unpracticed episodes, so the model's `CanMoveRoom` correctly forbids the reverse order. The unpracticed throw rates (35/200, 48/200) sit at the ~19–25% chance rate, confirming the horizon change to 12 does **not** reopen the retry channel: a trash retry still lands at step 13, and recycling is terminal at any horizon. The two structural risks were both checked rather than assumed: the recycling asymmetry survives (0/245 periods with a second attempt), and both the oracle and Fast Downward solve the newly-ordered EMPTY (300/300 and 200/200). Three follow-ups, deliberately **not** bundled here: 1. **Re-run the three Tossing Room experiments** — bringup's sampler-iteration arms, reset-frequency, reset-interval — before any of their numbers is quoted again, including their sweep-0 columns. The two most interesting questions on the other side: does the "sampler goes *below* chance for the first 500 transitions" regression survive, and does the 1000-iteration bimodality? Both have a clean mechanistic explanation in the defect this closes. 2. **Fix the "exactly one terminal failure family" prose** in the two reset logs and the two analysis docstrings, as its own change. It is now false, and the reset experiments are precisely the ones that lean on it. 3. **Rebase #70/#71** onto this. `environments/tossingroomsplit/` is a **verbatim fork, not a subclass** — nothing in it imports `environments/tossingroom/` — so none of this propagates for free, and #70's selling point ("diff the two files") goes false the moment this lands and the fork doesn't follow. It needs: `_apply_throw`'s capacity refusal; `trash_button`/`recycling_button` replacing `button`/`button_room` (and dropping `--button-room`); a per-bin `_apply_press` with the button id in `PRESS`'s `arg`; a `ButtonForBin` analogue; `BinEmpty` as precondition **and** delete effect on both `THROW_TRASH`/`THROW_RECYCLING`; `PRESS` split per bin with an item parameter and `ignore_effects` dropped; `initial_count_low`/`high` removed; `longest_shortest_solve` reworked for two buttons; plus its renderer and oracle. Eight of its test files break as written. And `scripts/tossingroomsplit_skill_traces.py`'s `_observe_throw` re-implements the landing condition and computes `prefilled = count >= 1`; it will silently report the wrong `landed` unless updated. I did **not** re-run any published experiment, and no number in the invalidation list has been re-measured — those are classifications of what the fix touches. <details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

# Implement Intelligent Review Synthesis Workflow

## Objective
Create an automated GitHub Actions workflow that synthesizes feedback from multiple AI code review bots (Sourcery, CodeRabbit, Copilot, Qodo) into a single, actionable report with smart deduplication, severity scoring, and follow-up issue generation.

## Requirements

### 1. Create Workflow File
Create `.github/workflows/review-synthesis.yml` with the following features:

#### Triggers
- `pull_request_review` (when bots submit reviews)
- `pull_request_review_comment` (when bots comment on code)
- `issue_comment` (when bots comment on PR)

#### Core Features

**A. Bot Comment Collection**
- Collect all comments/reviews from: `sourcery-ai[bot]`, `coderabbitai[bot]`, `Copilot[bot]`, `qodo-merge-pro[bot]`
- Support PR reviews, review comments, and issue comments
- Store collected data in JSON format

**B. Semantic Deduplication**
- Use `sentence-transformers` (model: `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) to create embeddings
- Cluster similar reviews using cosine similarity (threshold: 0.75)
- Group duplicate/similar feedback from multiple bots
- Track consensus count (how many bots reported the same issue)

**C. Severity Scoring Algorithm**
Implement weighted severity scoring (0-10 scale):

```python
Base Score by Keywords:
- Critical (10): security, vulnerability, exploit, injection, malicious
- High (7): error, bug, fail, crash, data loss, memory leak
- Medium (5): warning, issue, problem, performance, optimize
- Low (3): style, formatting, typo, suggestion

Consensus Multiplier: 1 + (consensus_count - 1) * 0.3
Final Score: min(10, base_score * consensus_multiplier)
```

**D. Category Detection**
Detect and tag reviews with categories:
- `security` (auth, encryption, vulnerabilities)
- `performance` (optimization, caching, memory)
- `code_quality` (maintainability, complexity, duplication)
- `bugs` (errors, crashes, incorrect behavior)
- `style` (formatting, naming, conventions)
- `documentation` (comments, docstrings, README)
- `testing` (test coverage, unit tests, mocks)
- `architecture` (design patterns, structure, SOLID)

**E. Actionability Detection**
Flag reviews as actionable if they contain:
- `should`, `must`, `need to`, `required`
- `fix`, `change`, `update`, `replace`
- `add`, `remove`, `refactor`, `implement`

**F. Generate Synthesis Report**
Create markdown report with:
- Summary statistics (counts by severity level)
- Critical issues section (always shown, full text)
- High priority issues (top 5, truncated if long)
- Actionable items summary (expandable details)
- Category breakdown (bar chart/list)
- Bot participation tracking
- Severity distribution

**G. Follow-Up Issue Generation**
Automatically create GitHub issues for:
- Top 3 items that are: (Critical OR High) AND Actionable
- Issue title format: `[SEVERITY] category - From PR #123`
- Issue body includes:
  - Source PR link
  - Severity score and level
  - Categories and consensus count
  - Full review text
  - Deduplicated similar reviews (collapsible)
- Labels: `bot-review`, `needs-triage`, severity labels, category labels

### 2. Dependencies
Install Python packages:
```
PyGithub
sentence-transformers
scikit-learn
numpy
```

### 3. Permissions Required
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
```

### 4. Report Features
- Update existing synthesis comment if found (don't spam)
- Link created follow-up issues back to PR
- Show deduplication rate: `(1 - unique_issues / total_comments) * 100%`

## Implementation Notes

1. **Semantic Similarity**: Use cosine similarity on sentence embeddings to cluster reviews. This catches:
   - Same issue reported by different bots in different words
   - Similar concerns about the same code section
   
2. **Consensus Weighting**: When 3+ bots flag the same issue, boost severity significantly. This indicates a real problem.

3. **Actionability Focus**: Prioritize reviews that tell you *what to do*, not just observations.

4. **Category Tagging**: Multi-label classification helps organize feedback by concern area.

5. **Performance**: Use lightweight model (`all-MiniLM-L6-v2`) for fast inference. Cache pip packages.

6. **Idempotency**: Update existing report comment instead of creating duplicates on re-runs.

## Expected Outcomes

For a PR with 17 bot comments (like PR #40):
- **Before**: 17 separate comments to read, many duplicates
- **After**: 
  - 1 synthesis report showing ~5-8 unique issues
  - Severity-ranked with consensus weights
  - 2-3 auto-created follow-up issues for critical items
  - Clear actionable recommendations

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Workflow triggers on bot reviews/comments
- [ ] Successfully deduplicates similar feedback
- [ ] Generates accurate severity scores
- [ ] Detects categories and actionability correctly
- [ ] Posts synthesis report as PR comment
- [ ] Creates follow-up issues for high-severity items
- [ ] Works with all 4 supported bots
- [ ] Runs within 3-5 minutes per PR

### Summary
This PR bundles three related multi-node bugs on quiz exercises that surfaced together on staging/production after the 9.0.1 Spring Boot 4 / Hibernate 7 upgrade:

1. **#12574 — MC selected options randomly appear deselected after refresh.** The refresh-path queries loaded `MultipleChoiceSubmittedAnswer.selectedOptions` polymorphically through the single-table `SubmittedAnswer` hierarchy with `@Cache(NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE)` active, which on a Hazelcast-backed multi-node cluster returned partial selections under concurrent read/write pressure. The stored `scoreInPoints` of submissions evaluated during the bug window could also collapse to 0.

2. **#12584 — Live quiz submission fails with `ObjectNotFoundException`.** `POST /api/quiz/exercises/{id}/submissions/live` accepted a raw `QuizSubmission` entity from the client and called `repository.save` directly. Hibernate's merge cascade tried to resolve every `AnswerOption` / `DragItem` / `DropLocation` / `ShortAnswerSpot` reference via `internalLoad(eager=true, nullable=false)` and — under the multi-node Hibernate-7 / JCache-bridged Hazelcast setup — intermittently threw `ObjectNotFoundException` for rows that exist in the DB, aborting the whole submission. Reproducible immediately on prod with a minimal fresh quiz.

3. **Edit screen vanishes after saving a new quiz.** After save, the client ended up displaying the "The quiz has started. No more changes allowed." warning for a not-yet-started quiz, because `onSaveSuccess` combined the server-provided `isEditable` flag with the local check — but the create/update endpoints don't populate `isEditable` on the response DTO, so `undefined && true` produced a falsy result.

### Motivation and Context
- #12574 — student-facing data-loss/scoring bug in MCQ quizzes. Reported on Q01E01 for INHN0006.
- #12584 — critical production regression: every live quiz submission on a multi-node deployment returned 500. Blocks quiz participation entirely.
- The "edit screen disappears" bug was introduced by the recent editability change (#12139) and affects instructors every time they create or edit a not-yet-started quiz.

No database migration is required. Scores of MC submissions that were auto-evaluated while #12574 was active may still be incorrect; an instructor can trigger **Re-evaluate** on an affected quiz to repair them — re-evaluation now reads the full selection.

### Description

**Fix for #12574 (selected options persistence):**
- `SubmittedAnswerRepository`: new `findMcSubmittedAnswersWithSelectedOptionsBySubmissionIds` query (dedicated `LEFT JOIN FETCH` for `selectedOptions`) and an `initializeSelectedOptionsForMultipleChoiceAnswers` default method that copies the fetched collections onto the in-memory submitted answers. The existing `loadQuizSubmissionsSubmittedAnswers` helper invokes it automatically, so every caller that uses it (exam conduction, quiz evaluation, statistics update, data export) is covered.
- `QuizParticipationResource`: calls `initializeSelectedOptionsForMultipleChoiceAnswers` in both the `start-participation` (POST) and the `participations/.../result` (GET) endpoints after the submission has been loaded.
- `QuizExerciseService.updateResultsOnQuizChanges` (used by instructor-triggered **Re-evaluate**): initializes selected options before `calculateAndUpdateScores` recomputes scores.
- `QuizStatisticService.recalculateStatistics` / `updateStatistics`: same treatment — the question-level statistics counters iterate `mcSubmittedAnswer.getSelectedOptions()` directly.
- `DataExportQuizExerciseCreationService.createQuizAnswersExport`: loads submissions for the per-question export that compares selectedOptions against answer options.
- `QuizSubmissionRepository.findWithEagerSubmittedAnswersByResultId`: added `DISTINCT` for defensiveness against the inner `JOIN submission.results` multiplying rows.
- Removed `@Cache(NONSTRICT_READ_WRITE)` from the three actively-mutated submitted-answer child collections (`MultipleChoiceSubmittedAnswer.selectedOptions`, `DragAndDropSubmittedAnswer.mappings`, `ShortAnswerSubmittedAnswer.submittedTexts`) — they are small, frequently re-written during autosave/evaluation, and the cache was actively producing partial reads rather than helping.

**Fix for #12584 (live submission crash):**
- `QuizSubmissionService.saveSubmissionForLiveMode`: load the quiz eagerly via `findByIdWithQuestionsElseThrow` (which brings every `AnswerOption` / `DragItem` / `DropLocation` / `ShortAnswerSpot` into the current persistence context) and sanitize each submitted answer against the server-side question set. Every client-supplied reference is replaced with the session-managed instance before `repository.save`; unknown ids are dropped. After sanitization, the merge cascade has nothing to resolve mid-flight — the `EntityType.resolve` → `internalLoad` path in the failure stack trace is no longer reachable. This matches Hibernate's own documented recommendation for merging detached references.
- Added a server integration test that injects a fabricated AnswerOption id into a live submission and asserts the request still returns 200 with the valid selections persisted.

**Fix for the post-save edit-screen banner:**
- `quiz-exercise-update.component.ts`: `onSaveSuccess` now recomputes `isEditable` purely client-side via `isQuizEditable(this.quizExercise)`, matching what `init()` already does on the GET path. The prior `this.quizExercise.isEditable && isQuizEditable(...)` collapsed to `undefined` because the create/update response does not carry the `isEditable` field.
- Added a spec that mimics the real server response shape (omitted `isEditable`) and asserts the edit screen stays open.

### Test Coverage
<!-- Please add the test coverages for all changed files modified in this PR here. You can generate the coverage table using one of these options: -->
<!-- 1. Run `npm run coverage:pr` to generate coverage locally by running only the affected module tests (see supporting_scripts/code-coverage/local-pr-coverage/README.md) -->
<!-- 2. Use `supporting_scripts/code-coverage/generate_code_cov_table/generate_code_cov_table.py` to generate the table from CI artifacts (requires GitHub token, follow the README for setup) -->

| quiz-exercise-update.component.ts | 93.00% | 656 | 248 | 37.8 |

_Last updated: 2026-04-23 09:26:52 UTC_


### Steps for Testing

#### #12574 — MC selected options persistence
Prerequisites:
- 1 Instructor, 1 Student
- 1 Course Quiz Exercise (SYNCHRONIZED) with at least one multiple-choice question that has several correct answer options

1. Log in as the instructor, create the quiz exercise, release and start it.
2. Log in as the student, participate in the quiz, select multiple answer options in the MC question, submit.
3. Wait until the quiz ends and the automatic evaluation has run (or trigger re-evaluation from the instructor UI).
4. As the student, reload the quiz page repeatedly (at least 5–10 times).
5. Verify that **all** originally selected answer options stay selected on every reload and that the per-question score stays at its evaluated value (e.g. 1/1 for a fully correct MC answer).
6. As the instructor, trigger **Re-evaluate** — the per-question score must remain correct (previously it could flip to 0).

##### Exam Mode
Prerequisites: 1 Instructor, 1 Student, 1 Exam with an MC quiz exercise.
1. Conduct the exam as the student, select options for the MC quiz, submit the exam.
2. After the exam ends and results are published, reload the result screen multiple times.
3. Verify the selected options and the per-question score are stable across reloads.

#### #12584 — Live submission no longer crashes (multi-node)
Prerequisites:
- Multi-node Artemis deployment (staging1)
- 1 Instructor, 1 Student, 1 freshly created SYNCHRONIZED quiz with at least one MC question

1. As the student, open the quiz and select one or more answer options.
2. Autosave fires (or click submit). On prior builds this returned 500 with `ObjectNotFoundException: AnswerOption ...` in the server log.
3. Verify the request returns 200 and the selection persists across refresh.
4. Repeat with DnD and SA questions to cover the other two submitted-answer types.

#### Edit screen stays visible after saving a new quiz
1. Log in as instructor, create a new quiz exercise (or open an existing not-yet-started one).
2. Make any edit and click **Save**.
3. Verify the edit form stays visible — the "The quiz has started. No more changes allowed." banner must **not** appear.

  * Preserve client-side editability state after save rather than deferring to server flag.

…e notebook

The notebook did not survive Restart & Run All, and one dead cell reported another model's score as its own. Fixes verified by a full fresh-kernel run: 0 errors, execution counts 1..83 strictly increasing, 483s.

Failures
- Port the neural network from TensorFlow/Keras to PyTorch. TF publishes no wheel for Python 3.14, so the section could never run; torch was already in the kernel. Both `!pip install` cells removed.
- Cell 163 printed the Gradient Boosting RMSE (9028.98) under the Neural Networks heading, because the dead cell left `y_pred_scaled` bound to the GBR predictions. Predictions are now named per model.
- Drop max_features='auto' from the GBR grid: removed in scikit-learn 1.3, it silently scored 36 of 108 candidates NaN. An assert now fails loudly instead.
- Residual plots no longer subtract standardised predictions from USD targets.
- Remove the second target scaler that the PCA section applied incorrectly.

Correctness
- Drop `Property Age`: verified byte-for-byte duplicate of `Income (USD)` on all 25,150 rows where both are present. Withdraws the "high income people live in older properties" claim, which was a column correlated with itself.
- Model the 26.8% of rejected applicants instead of deleting them: a two-stage approval classifier x amount regressor. End-to-end R2 0.7803 vs 0.4204 for the single-regressor design.
- Move imputation and scaling into a Pipeline fitted per fold on training data only; stop overwriting 361 real target labels with the column mean.
- One-hot encode nominal categories instead of LabelEncoder, so the linear and PCA models are not handicapped by an invented ordering.
- Share one preprocessor across all five models so the comparison is like for like; report explicit baselines (best model is 24.9% below the best of them).
- Delete dead KNN imputation code that contradicted the markdown.

Add README.md and requirements.txt for the setup instructions the submission requires, and NOTEBOOK_REVIEW.md as the audit trail.

## Description

This PR addresses issue #47 by adding comprehensive benchmarking and documentation for succinctly's rank/select implementation against other maintained Rust succinct-structure crates (vers-vecs, sucds, and sux). The work includes both empirical measurements and an Architecture Decision Record (ADR-0011) that records the build-vs-buy reasoning behind implementing custom succinct structures in-crate rather than depending on existing libraries.

Prior to this PR, the repository could not answer whether existing crates were evaluated or benchmarked. The documentation incorrectly claimed ~3% space overhead for the rank directory (the Poppy paper's figure, not this implementation's). This PR corrects the record with measured data and honest assessment of trade-offs.

## Type of Change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) — `succinct_libs` benchmark suite
- [x] Documentation update — ADR-0011, benchmark page, corrected space overhead claims
- [x] Test coverage improvement — comparison verification in benchmark

## Related Issue
Fixes #47 — "Evaluate existing succinct crates and benchmark against them"

## Changes Made

**Benchmark Implementation:**
- Added `bench-compare/benches/succinct_libs.rs` with comprehensive rank/select comparison across four libraries
- Implemented `TrackingAllocator` for precise resident-size measurement
- Created `verify_agreement` test ensuring all four libraries agree on rank1/select1 answers before timing
- Benchmarks test construction, rank1 (10,000 random queries), select1, and resident memory across 1M-10M bits at 10/50/90% density
- Added `succinct_libs` benchmark to registry in `src/bin/succinctly/bench_runner/registry.rs`
- Updated `bench-compare/Cargo.toml` with dependencies: `vers-vecs`, `sucds`, `sux`, `rand`, `rand_chacha` (all pinned for reproducibility)
- Updated `bench-compare/Cargo.toml` to enable `simd` feature for succinctly and vers-vecs

**Documentation:**
- Created `docs/adrs/adr-0011.md` — Architecture Decision Record documenting why succinct structures are built in-crate
  - Records three requirements: `no_std` support (no existing crate satisfies), balanced-parentheses tree navigation (none provide), hinted select (none expose)
  - Honestly reports that BitVec wins no measured category on ARM64: sux is 1.5-1.7x faster at rank/select, vers-vecs is 5-8x more compact and faster to build
  - Documents why BitVec is kept despite losing: only `no_std` requirement currently holds; BalancedParens and JsonIndex bypass BitVec entirely
  - Lists alternatives evaluated and rejected (vers-vecs, sux, sucds, succinct, fid, bio) with rationale
- Created `docs/benchmarks/rust-succinct-libs.md` — benchmark results and methodology
  - Platforms: ARM64 only (Apple M5 Max); flags x86_64 run as outstanding
  - Resident size table: vers-vecs 5-8x more compact; succinctly 27.5-47.5% overhead rising with density
  - Construction: vers-vecs 1.0-1.31x faster
  - rank1: succinctly 1.8-2.3x faster than vers-vecs, but sux 1.5-1.7x faster than succinctly
  - select1: sux 3-4x faster; marked as noisy (~40% variance in individual cells)
  - Documents fairness caveat: sucds/sux lack bulk-word constructor, must fill per-bit
- Updated `docs/adrs/README.md` to add ADR-0011 entry
- Updated `docs/architecture/README.md` — noted Prior Art now includes Rust crates evaluated
- Corrected `docs/architecture/bitvec.md` — rank directory overhead documented as ~25% (128 bits per 512 bits), not ~3%; full BitVec 27.5-47.5% resident
- Comprehensively updated `docs/architecture/prior-art.md`
  - Clarified Poppy paper claims 3% but succinctly's directory costs ~25% by design
  - Added table of Rust succinct libraries with versions, `no_std` status, and assessments
  - Documented sucds `no_std` attribute is vestigial in 0.8.3 — builds fail with ~141 errors
  - Cross-referenced ADR-0011 and benchmark page
- Updated `docs/benchmarks/README.md` — added rust-succinct-libs row to benchmark table
- Updated `docs/benchmarks/inventory.md` — added rust-succinct-libs.md (4 sections)
- Updated `docs/log.md` with 2026-07-15 entry documenting sources ingested and corrections made
- Updated `docs/optimizations/cache-memory.md` — rank directory overhead corrected from 3% to ~25%
- Updated `docs/optimizations/hierarchical-structures.md` — rank/select overhead corrected to reflect actual measurements
- Updated `CLAUDE.md` — BitVec performance summary corrected from ~3-4% to ~28-48% overhead
- Updated `README.md` — corrected feature claims from "~3% space overhead" to "tuned for query speed over compactness (~28-48% overhead)"
- Updated README core structures documentation with link to benchmark results

## Testing

**Automated Testing:**
- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] New benchmark suite added with verification step (`verify_agreement` ensures all four libraries agree on rank1/select1 answers)
- [x] Benchmark registered and accessible via `bench run succinct_libs` command

**Manual Testing:**
- [x] Benchmarks tested on ARM64 (Apple M5 Max)
- [x] `cargo test` passes with all benchmarks
- [x] `cargo clippy` clean
- [x] `cargo fmt` applied

### Test Commands
```bash
# Run the new benchmark suite
cd bench-compare
cargo bench --bench succinct_libs

# Or via the bench runner
succinctly bench run succinct_libs

# Verify all tests pass
cargo test --all

# Check code quality
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

## Performance Impact
- [x] No performance impact to main crate (benchmarks are in `bench-compare` standalone crate)
- Benchmark findings documented: succinctly's BitVec trades space for query speed; loses on space (vers-vecs 5-8x better), loses on select (sux 3-4x faster), competitive on rank, faster to build than sux/sucds

## Checklist
- [x] My code follows the project's style guidelines
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have added comprehensive documentation explaining the decision
- [x] Benchmark code includes verification logic (`verify_agreement`)
- [x] New and existing tests pass locally
- [x] Documentation is complete and accurate (corrected prior misstated overhead figures)
- [x] No new warnings generated

## Additional Notes

**Honest Assessment**: This PR deliberately reports findings as they came out rather than as a defense of the existing code. The measurements show BitVec loses on space and select performance but wins on rank speed (among the measured libraries). The decision to keep it in-crate is justified by three requirements: `no_std` (which no external crate satisfies), balanced-parentheses tree navigation, and hinted select — only the first currently applies to BitVec itself. The code acknowledges that BalancedParens and JsonIndex bypass BitVec entirely, making its use a candidate for replacement (tracked in issue #228).

**Platform Limitations**: Results are ARM64-only (Apple M5 Max). Succinctly's x86_64 popcount is AVX-512 VPOPCNTDQ-gated and untested here. Vers-vecs' SIMD select is also AVX-512-gated, so an x86_64 run could change the placings and is flagged as outstanding. The resident-size measurements are deterministic and platform-independent.

**Space Overhead Corrections**: Four documents claimed ~3% overhead for the rank directory. That is the Poppy paper's figure, not succinctly's implementation. All instances have been corrected to the measured value: ~25% for the rank directory alone, 27.5-47.5% for the full BitVec with select index (rising with density). This was an arithmetic error in bitvec.md that propagated through the docs.

**Future Work**: ADR-0011 recommends revisiting this decision if the `no_std` requirement is dropped or if sucds fixes its `no_std` build. The benchmark provides a stable baseline for that future evaluation.

reviews.body:
## What

A full staleness audit and repair of `docs/` + `README.md`, requested as a fresh-eyes review of the doc folder. No engine code changes (`examples/verify_sql_reference.rs` gained 4 verifier statements; 33/33 pass).

One systemic disease, found in **both directions**: content sections got patched when features shipped, but the cross-cutting scaffolding — indexes, status headers, version stamps, footers — did not. 4 registry rows were behind their item files, and 19 item files were behind their (correct) registry rows.

## Correctness fixes (claims that were actively false)

| Doc | Was | Is |
|---|---|---|
| `engine_design.md` | `FORMAT_VERSION` **8**; live vector index described as IVF-Flat in 3 sections; constraints "pending merge"; module map missing `authz/`/`backup/`/`replication/` | **12** with v9→v12 history from `src/format.rs`; HNSW everywhere with dated corrections; items 35/36 reality; full module map; §12 gap registry corrected; 2026-07-22 closeout ledger entry |
| `ops_runbook.md` | "unidb does not prune logs"; §3 said time-PITR is a follow-up while §9 documented it shipped | Server prunes at `UNIDB_LOG_RETAIN_DAYS` (default **7**) — day-7 loss risk called out; PITR contradiction fixed; **new vacuum/autovacuum section** (5 knobs + metrics); missing env vars added |
| `engine_access_guide.md` | Told users 6 **shipped** features were "not supported" (window fns, FULL OUTER/NATURAL JOIN, set ops, RETURNING, …); never named `execute_sql_as`/`execute_cypher`/`ReadHandle` | Corrected + entry points documented + item-111 grant-filtered `information_schema` explained |
| `sql_reference.md` | Denied CTEs and `JOIN … ON` (both supported + tested); `INCLUDE` and `HAVING` undocumented; overstated verifier claim | Corrected with inline notes; new WITH section; covering-index docs; verifier claim honest and extended (**33/33 OK**) |
| `REST_API.md` | `PUT /config/group_commit_window_us` (item 101) missing | Documented |
| `README.md` | "postgres 14×" on UPDATE (reality: unidb **1.06×** HOT-eligible); crash count 44; feature list missing window fns/full-text/set ops | Official 2026-07-21 report numbers; 54 crash tests; feature list completed |
| `positioning.md` | Pre-Phase-6 snapshot: "no window functions", auth "in progress", replication "not shipped" | Post-Phase-6 reality; honest remaining gaps kept (no triggers/views/procedures, single-primary) |

## Bookkeeping

- `backlog_index.md` rows **107/109/110/111**: `NOT STARTED` → `SHIPPED` (PRs #196–#199 — the registry claimed a high-severity RLS crash was unaddressed when it was fixed); dead crossed-out "Next up" replaced with the live 2026-07-22 priorities.
- **19 item-file Status headers** flipped to match their registry rows (27/34/45/51/52/61/62/66–69/74/91/93/96–99/101/107), each with a dated correction note.
- Orphan duplicate-ID file `42_fk_error_message_direction.md` (unregistered OPEN bug) renumbered → **item 113** and registered; the bug is verified still live (`src/error.rs::fk_violation_msg` has only the child-direction message). Next ID → 114.
- 0-byte `engine_internals_doc_prompt.md` (committed empty since 2026-07-09, cited as a real meta doc) given honest content.
- `roadmap.md`, `design_index.md`, `storage_service.md`, `item28_design.md`, processing-engines index: markers, missing entries, staleness notices.

## Structure

- `documentation_index.md` rebuilt by audience (app builders / operators / engine engineers) — it previously omitted `ops_runbook.md` and `positioning.md` entirely and falsely called the performance reports "git-ignored".
- New `docs/performance/README.md`: the four report families + which of the 30 dated reports is the authoritative baseline (`report_20260721_035629.md`) + the item-108 cross-run-ratio caveat.
- **New `scripts/lint_backlog.sh`** — mechanically cross-checks every numbered file's Status header against its registry row, catches orphans and duplicate IDs. Clean pass on all 89 files; wired into the index's update instructions. This guard would have caught today's entire drift class automatically.

## Reviewer notes

- Every correction follows §9: dated inline correction notes, never silent rewrites; historical footer/ledger entries left untouched.
- Benchmark numbers quoted are only from the committed official record (`report_20260721_035629.md`); no new measurements were run.
- Per §6 this is a docs-only PR — no benchmark table applies; no locked decision (§3) touched.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

reviews.body:
Phase 0 of the launch-readiness work: the parts a stranger sees first.

## Brand assets (`assets/`)
The Marshal crown, hand-authored as SVG in four variants (light, dark, `currentColor` mono, wordmark) plus a flat architecture diagram. Palette and intended use documented in `assets/README.md`. Verified legible at 32x32.

## README
Restructured as a landing page rather than a manual, following the shape Ruff, uv and Zed use: identity, then proof, then install, then a working example.

- The measured benchmark table moves above the fold. It is the argument, so it goes first.
- Install leads with `uv tool install MarshalFleet` / `pipx`; clone-from-source moves to `SETUP.md`.
- A "60 seconds" walkthrough with real captured output from `doctor`, `spawn` and `status`.
- A comparison table against hand-rolled worktree scripts, in-harness subagents, and generic workflow orchestrators.
- The backend matrix now lists all seven adapters with their model flag and cost provenance.

Net 138 lines shorter. The defensive caveat paragraph became a neutral "what a run returns" note in `docs/usage.md`; the cost-provenance explainer moved to `docs/model-playbook.md`.

## `docs/nerds.md`
New home for the material the README no longer carries: benchmark methodology, the cost-provenance taxonomy, the permission-fidelity matrix, and the worktree-isolation threat model.

## Hygiene
- `.commandcode/` untracked and added to `.gitignore` (same class of local tooling state as `.claude/`).
- `docs/status.md` claimed eight adapters including a `gemini.py` that does not exist; corrected to seven, and the contradictory duplicate "Remaining:" paragraph removed.

Gate green: 1082 passed, 92% coverage, ruff and mypy clean.

reviews.title: release: v0.11.2

reviews.body:
## Performance

Measured with `benchmarks/`, which drives a real `WebSocketSession` against an out-of-process feeder over loopback. Medians are corrected for machine speed using controls recorded in the same run (a raw recv loop with no session); the residual disagreement between those controls after correction is ±9%, so smaller changes below are not claims.

| channel | before | after | msg/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `orderbook.BTC-PERP.1.20` | 28.3 µs | 10.7 µs | 35.4k → 93.2k |
| `ticker_slim.BTC-PERP.100` | 19.7 µs | 7.5 µs | 50.7k → 133.2k |
| `trades.BTC-PERP` (20 trades) | 38.1 µs | 15.5 µs | 26.3k → 64.5k |

Two changes account for it, both confirmed by how the saving scales:

- **Handler dispatch** (2021114) saves ~9–11 µs per message regardless of payload size, consistent with removing two task creations and a semaphore acquisition per message. This also fixes a correctness bug: handlers no longer race each other, so per-channel ordering is preserved.
- **Single-pass notification decode** (8a1ee38) saves 3–10.5 µs scaling with payload size, consistent with removing a full dict materialisation of every payload before converting it.

Remaining per-message time is roughly 35% `websockets` recv, 55% msgspec decode, 10% this library.

Caveats: loopback, no TLS, no-op handler, synthetic payloads generated from the channel schemas. `python -m benchmarks history --base <base>` reproduces the table; `benchmarks/README.md` documents the method.

## What changed

**Root README restructure, plain-English first:**
- The intro now leads with a performance highlight (hinted 0.2–0.4 s, blind ~0.5 s, matched or beat ASTAP on every workload we tested) linking down to the full Performance section, which keeps all the benchmark tables and caveats.
- A "Try it without installing anything" callout points at the hosted solver at [seiza.fyi](https://seiza.fyi), which the CLI worker can also target with `seiza worker --server`.
- New **Install** (MSI / RPM+deb / cargo) and **Ways to use it** (N.I.N.A., application worker, Rust crates) sections sit right after the intro, written in direct how-to language.
- Quick start, `seiza setup`, and the worker paragraphs were rewritten in the same plain voice; the nerdy bundle/compatibility detail moved under its own "Catalogs and data" heading with a "most users only need prebuilt/setup" lead.

**Documentation brought current with shipped work:**
- Root and `seiza` crate READMEs now describe the extensible v4 object container: preserved upstream records, typed relations, facet selections, source-qualified geometry (incl. OpenNGC outlines), pinned provenance, curated corrections, and `seiza catalog object --all-sources`.
- Layout section lists the full workspace (`seiza-download`, `seiza-sources`, `packaging/windows`, `docs` were missing).
- `seiza-fits` README gains the planar RGB (`NAXIS3`) and `BAYERPAT` debayering bullet (verified in `bayer.rs`).
- "Planned" no longer lists the blind pattern index, which shipped as `blind-gaia16.idx`.

**Stale design-doc statuses corrected:**
- `astap-mode.md`: "implementation not started" → implemented.
- `fits-streaming-io.md`: drops the merged `codex/fits-streaming` branch reference.
- `objects-bin-v3.md`: v4 is no longer a "successor proposal" — it is the written format, with v3 embedded as its required hot section and still writable via `write_v3_to`.

Follow-up to #13. Benchmarking showed the NVML switch left most of its win on the table: an \`nvmlInit\`/\`nvmlShutdown\` cycle costs **~9 ms** while the queries themselves take **~1.4 ms**, so tearing the session down on every poll was the dominant cost.

## Change
Initialise NVML once behind a lock and keep the session for the process lifetime. The cached session is dropped only if device enumeration fails, so a driver reload still recovers on the next poll. Per-field \`NOT_SUPPORTED\` handling is unchanged.

Keeping the session open costs **no extra memory** — the driver library's pages stay resident after first load either way (verified below).

## Measured on the GB10 (andromeda)

\`get_gpu()\`, 30 calls:

| Implementation | Mean | Spread |
|---|---|---|
| \`nvidia-smi\` (1.0.0) | 26.7 ms | 24.4–29.1 ms |
| NVML, init/shutdown per call (1.0.1) | 19.4 ms | 18.7–20.3 ms |
| **NVML, cached session (this PR)** | **1.28 ms** | 1.24–1.53 ms |

**~21× faster than \`nvidia-smi\`**, ~15× faster than 1.0.1.

RSS is flat — **not** a leak, and caching adds nothing:

| Calls | 100 | 400 | 1000 |
|---|---|---|---|
| RSS | 67.3 MiB | 67.3 MiB | 67.3 MiB |

End-to-end \`/api/metrics\` on the real container: Docker-disabled **~40 ms → ~12 ms**. All-categories stays ~2.0 s (Docker's stats sampling sets that floor regardless of the GPU path).

## README
The resource table was stale, so it is re-measured against this build:
- Memory \`~41/44 MiB\` → **~57 MiB** (the resident NVIDIA driver library; fixed cost, does not grow with uptime)
- \`/api/metrics\` all categories \`~1.1 s\` → **~2.0 s**
- \`/api/metrics\` Docker disabled \`~50 ms\` → **~12 ms**
- New row for GPU collection alone (~1.3 ms)
- DCGM comparison corrected **~14× → ~10×** memory, since our own memory figure went up

Verified by running this code in the production container on andromeda, then restoring it to stock 1.0.1.

The [Red Hat blog post published today](https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/policy-code-what-happens-when-you-layer-policy-enforcement-automation-you-already-have) links this repository directly. That makes the README a landing page for public traffic, so I audited every claim in it against the actual tree.

## 1. Broken paths — 11 of them

Every Linux CIS benchmark was documented under `benchmarks/cis/os/linux/<os>/`. **That directory does not exist.** The real layout is `benchmarks/cis/<os>/`. What *is* under `os/linux/` is `rhel_9_legacy/` and `rhel_9_simple/`.

The CIS RHEL 9 **coverage badge pointed at one of these** — so the single most likely first click from the blog was a 404.

| Documented | Actual |
|---|---|
| `benchmarks/cis/os/linux/{rhel_8,rhel_9,ubuntu_*,debian_11,rocky_linux_8,amazon_linux_2023}/` | `benchmarks/cis/<os>/` |
| `benchmarks/cis/os/windows/` | `benchmarks/cis/windows_server_2022_modular/` |
| `frameworks/federal/nist_800_53/` | `frameworks/federal/nist/sp_800_53/` |
| `frameworks/federal/nist_800_82/` | `frameworks/critical_infrastructure/nist_800_82/` |
| `frameworks/management/ncsc_caf/` | `frameworks/compliance/ncsc_caf/` |

All **40** referenced paths now resolve against `main`.

## 2. Three different policy counts, none correct

| Source | Claimed |
|---|---|
| Repo description | 461 |
| README header | 505 |
| Domain table sum | 461 |
| **Actual on main** | **532** (613 incl. tests) |

Domain rows corrected to 273 / 225 / 14 / 19 / 1 — which now sums to 532.

## 3. The 100% claim

A brightgreen `338/338 (100%)` badge sat at the top, repeated three more times.

**338 is the size of the CIS RHEL 9 benchmark** — true, and kept as the why-not-build-your-own argument. It is **not** our measured coverage. The modules reference **224 distinct CIS control IDs**.

224 is a *floor, not a ceiling* — one rule often satisfies several controls — so the README now says `224+ across 17 modules` and ships the command that reproduces it from a clone. A reader who checks now finds the number reconciles, which was not previously true.

## 4. Under-claiming

Nine shipped benchmarks weren't in the coverage table at all: RHEL 10, Rocky 8/9, Debian 11, Amazon Linux 2023, Windows 10/11, Microsoft 365, PostgreSQL, VyOS/pfSense.

## Also

- **Private repo linked publicly** — the README linked `ynotbhatc/compliance`, which 404s for every public reader. Now named without a link.
- **LICENSE misdetected** — it was Apache 2.0 with the appendix replaced by a filled-in copyright, so GitHub classified it `other` instead of `Apache-2.0`. Restored to canonical text; copyright preserved **verbatim** in `NOTICE`, where Apache 2.0 puts attribution. **No change to licensing terms** — but it is a legal file, so worth an eyeball.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** carried the same wrong paths and stale count — that's how the drift reached the README. Fixed so the next contributor inherits the real layout.

## Deliberately NOT fixed — needs your call

`benchmarks/cis/rhel_9/cis_rhel9_complete.rego:196` hardcodes:

```rego
total_controls_covered := 338
```

and the report emits `"total_controls": 338`. **This is the root of the 100% claim.** Changing it would shift every compliance percentage already stored in PostgreSQL and break historical comparison, so I left it alone rather than silently rewriting scoring behaviour.

```
broken paths: 0    stale counts: 0    domain table sums to 532 ✅
```

reviews.body:
## What

Fixes the **"red veil"** rendering bug and refreshes the benchmark at the corrected prompt.

### The bug
The scene-extraction prompt left `backdrop.color` with **no neutral default**. On a request that named no backdrop, the LLM invented a color (often **red**), which — with a gray world and white lights — bled a colored cast over otherwise-neutral packshots.

### The fix
- `product_render_extractor.py`: honor **any named backdrop shade** (including gray nuances `cool_gray` / `warm_gray` / `neutral_gray`); fall back to `neutral_gray` **only** when no backdrop is described.
- `index.html`: Console presets now name their backdrop explicitly.

A first, over-aggressive wording regressed `v0-sphere` ("fond gris froid" → overridden to neutral_gray); the shipped version fixes that — verified on the benchmark.

### Proof
- Two product renders (no backdrop named) → `neutral_gray` / `cool_gray`, **no red cast** (visual + IR).
- Full suite: **1629 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed**.

### Benchmark refresh (idle machine, honest timing)
- `product_render` (coder:7b): **0.876 → 0.905**; `backdrop.color` 0.900→1.000, `pedestal.color` 0.000→1.000; `schema_version` 0.545 unchanged (remaining systemic gap).
- Cross-model (6 models) re-measured: the **default 7b now ties the 14b for best quality (0.905) while running 1.4× faster** → "the default is the right call" is now unambiguous.
- 5-seed reproducibility: **bit-identical** (stdev 0.000).
- `BENCHMARK.md`, README table, and the quality-vs-speed slide regenerated.

## Commits
1. `fix(render)` — the fix + benchmark refresh + slide.
2. `docs(readme)` — README rework + Console hero + benchmark table.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

+- **The default is the right call — now unambiguously.** `qwen2.5-coder:7b` is **tied for the best quality** (0.905, with the 14 B) while running **1.4× faster**. It is the best quality *and* the best quality-per-second among the strong models. The model choice is *evidence-backed*, not assumed.

+- **Returns flatten, they don't just diminish.** 3b → 7b → 14b reads 0.785 → 0.905 → **0.905**: the 14 B adds **nothing** over the 7 B on this corpus, for 1.4× the latency. At this scale, paying for more parameters buys no quality.

+- **Code fine-tuning earns its keep.** `coder:7b` (0.905, 100 % parse) beats the *same-base, same-size* generalist `qwen2.5:7b` (0.809, 90.9 % parse) by **+0.096**. A controlled result: the only variable is the code tuning.

## Summary

`docs/root-static/llms.txt` and `docs/root-static/llms-full.txt` describe RF-DETR as an object detection **and instance segmentation** model only. Neither contains any keypoint content — no task listing, no usage snippet, no benchmark row, no API-reference link:

```
before:
  llms.txt       detection ✓  segmentation ✓  keypoint ✗
  llms-full.txt  detection ✓  segmentation ✓  keypoint ✗
after:
  llms.txt       detection ✓  segmentation ✓  keypoint ✓
  llms-full.txt  detection ✓  segmentation ✓  keypoint ✓
```

These files are served at `/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` specifically so assistants can ingest them. As written, an assistant asked *"does RF-DETR support keypoint detection?"* would answer **no** — while the project's own title is "Real-Time SOTA Object Detection, Instance Segmentation, **and Keypoint Detection**".

Neither file is generated. `.github/workflows/publish-docs.yml:144` copies them verbatim to the gh-pages root, so they silently drifted when keypoint support was added.

## Changes

**`llms.txt`** — keypoints added to the summary line, `Tasks:` list, Getting Started, Benchmarks, Model Selection Answers, and API Reference (model class + train config).

**`llms-full.txt`** — keypoints added to the summary line, Overview, and licensing list, plus:

- a new **`## Run Keypoints`** section (usage snippet, model class, preview caveat, `rfdetr`-package-only note), mirroring the existing Run Detection / Run Segmentation sections
- a new **`### Keypoint Results`** benchmark table matching the one in `docs/learn/benchmarks.md`

## Verification

- [x] Every numeric cell cross-checked against the README tables. The 12 pre-existing detection/segmentation rows already matched **exactly** and are untouched — this PR adds rows, it does not change any existing number.
- [x] All three new documentation URLs verified to resolve to real pages (`docs/learn/run/keypoints.md`, `docs/reference/kp_preview.md`, `docs/reference/keypoint_train_config.md`).
- [x] `pre-commit` passes on both files (whitespace, EOF, line endings, codespell).

## Merge order

Uses **40.7 M** for keypoint params — the corrected value from #1258. Until that lands, `README.md` still shows `126.4 M` (which is RF-DETR-XL's count, copied by mistake). Merging #1258 first avoids a window where the two disagree; there are no file conflicts between the PRs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

The previous README opened with a feature list — package name, CLI name, module entry point — which says nothing about why the project is worth reading. It was also the last Chinese document in the repository.

Rewritten in English around the actual argument: the tool loop is not the differentiator, the per-run record is. Adds the turn diagram, the termination rule and why `attempts` and `tool_steps` are separate counters, the six safety invariants, and the artifact contract.

**Every figure was checked against the code rather than carried over from the old text.** That check corrected three inaccuracies the draft had inherited or introduced:

- the REPL also accepts `/quit`
- both the OpenAI and Anthropic key chains fall back to *each other's* variables, which the old provider table truncated
- the benchmark is five named categories (documentation, text-edit, tool-boundary, recovery, durable-contract), not the loose list the draft listed

Limits are stated in the README itself rather than left implied: no external public benchmark, no live-provider evaluation, and a recorded archive that measures harness behaviour under a deterministic client rather than model capability.

+`attempts < max(max_steps * 3, max_steps + 4)`. The two counters are deliberately

+2. **Approval gate.** Risky tools require approval, and `read_only=True` denies
+3. **Deterministic patching.** `patch_file` requires `old_text` to occur exactly once.
+4. **Filtered shell environment.** `run_shell` receives an allowlist, not the inherited

+6. **Redaction.** Secret-shaped values never reach the trace, the report, or durable
